ANSWERED ON MONDAY , AUGUST 03, 2026 
 
Refund of depositors' money 
2517. Shri Bajrang Manohar Sonwane: 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that large amounts invested by 
citizens in cooperative credit societies, investment companies and other 
financial institutions have remained blocked for several years due to 
closure of such institutions or ongoing liquidation proceedings; 
(b) if so, the measures taken by the Government to ensure refund of 
depositors' money and the policy regarding attachment and sale of 
assets of such institutions for repayment to investors; 
(c) whether many investors have received only partial payments, if so, 
the time-bound plan for payment of the remaining amount; 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to prevent delays by 
Liquidators and ensure timely justice to depositors; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to establish Fast Track Courts or 
Special Courts for day-to-day hearing and speedy disposal of such cases 
in coordination with State Governments, including Maharashtra, to 
ensure early recovery of investors' dues and if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and Minister of 
State in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 
 (Shri Harsh Malhotra) 
 
(a) to ( d): (i) The Ministry of Corporate Affairs is responsible for the 
administration of Companies Act, 2013 (the Act) and the Insolvency and 
Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (the IBC). The Act provides the legal framework 
for acceptance of deposits, protection of depositors' interests and 
enforcement against defaults. Companies accepting deposits are 

required to comply with the provisions of Chapter V of the Companies 
Act, 2013 and the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014. In 
cases of non -compliance, appropriate action is taken under the 
provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, wherever warranted.  
(ii) Official Liquidators (OLs) are appointed under Section 448(1) of the 
Companies Act, 1956 for performance of duties as Liquidators of the 
companies ordered to be compulsorily wound up as per the orders of the 
Hon’ble High Court. As OL is an officer of the Hon'ble High Court, all 
activities including disbursement of money to the deposit holders, 
eventually leading towards dissolution of the company are carried out 
by OL, under the supervision of the Hon’ble High Court.  
 
(iii) IBC provides a consolidated framework for reorganization, 
insolvency resolution and liquidation of corporate persons . Under  
Section 227, the IBC enables the Central Government to notify Financial 
Service Providers ( FSPs) and categories of FSPs for the purpose of 
insolvency and liquidation proceedings. 
Till now, CIRPs of four FSPs have yielded resolutions under the IBC and 
one FSP is ongoing under the IBC. No liquidation has been ordered under 
the IBC in respect of any Financial Service Provider (FSP). 
 
(iv) As per inputs received from Ministry of Cooperation, Cooperative 
societies registered under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative 
Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 function as autonomous cooperative 
organisations and are accountable to their members. The affairs of such 
societies are governed by the provisi ons of the MSCS Act, 2002, the 
rules made thereunder and their approved bye-laws.  
The details of cooperative societies under Liquidation, powers of 
Liquidators and the details of repayments are provided as Annexure A.  
(e) In view of the reply above, no such proposal is under consideration 
of this Ministry. 
 
******* 
  

Annexure A 
Annexure referred in reply to Part (a to d) of the unstarred Question No. 2517 for 
answer in Lok Sabha on 03.08.2026. 
The details of cooperative societies under Liquidation, powers of Liquidators and the 
details of repayments:  
Presently, 115 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are under liquidation. Under Section 90 
of the MSCS Act, 2002, the Liquidator is empowered to refund the deposited amounts to 
depositors after realization of the assets of the society, settlement of liabilit ies and 
distribution of the assets among eligible depositors/members and other stakeholders. 
Further, in respect of the Sahara Group of Cooperative Societies, pursuant to the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court's order dated 29.03.2023, out of the amount of ₹24,979.67 crore lying in 
the "Sahara-SEBI Refund Account" , ₹10,000 crore has been transferred to the Central 
Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) for disbursement to genuine depositors. The 
CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal was launched on 18.07.2023 to facilitate online submission 
of refund claims by genuine depositors. Till 28th July, 2026, approximately ₹9,2 65 crore 
has been disbursed to around 41.50 lakh depositors of the four Sahara Cooperative 
Societies.

entries.t: Rural Unemployment Statistics and Employment Initiatives
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2518 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03RD AUGUST, 2026 
 
RURAL UNEMPLOYMENT STATISTICS AND EMPLOYMENT INITIATIVES 
 
2518.      MS. MAHUA MOITRA: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of all -India rural Current Weekly Status unemployment rate 
as per the latest Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS); 
(b) the details of unemployment rate of youth aged 15 to 29 years in rural 
areas of the country as per the said survey; 
(c) whether the youth unemployment in the rural areas of the country 
remains in double digits and if so, the reasons therefor; 
(d) the trend in the said youth unemployment figure during the last five 
PLFS cycles; and 
(e) the details of specific employment generation schemes, with budget 
allocation, targeted at reducing rural youth unemployment in 2025-26? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India are 
derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by the 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. The PLFS 
methodology was revamped with effect from January 2025. The PLFS Annual 
Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to present labour market 
estimates, covering the period from January to December 2025. 
 
As per PLFS reports, the estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) on current 
weekly status for persons of age 15 years and above has decreased from 5.0% 
in 2022 to 4.6% in 2025 in the rural areas of the country. 
Also, the estimated UR for youth of age 15 -29 years on usual status has 
decreased from 8.9% in 2022 to 8.3% in 2025 in the rural areas of the country. 
Further, the overall estimated UR for youth of age 15 -29 years has decreased 
from 10.9% in 2022 to 9.9% in 2025 in the country. 
 

Employment generation coupled with improving employability for youth is 
a priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing various 
employment generation schemes/ programmes like Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya 
Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY), Prime Minister’s Employment 
Generation Programme (PMEGP), Rural Self Employment and Training Institutes 
(RSETIs), Viksit Bharat –Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) 
etc. in the country (including for rural youth). The details of various 
employment generation schemes/ programmes being implemented by the 
Government may be seen at   https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
Additionally, Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) to 
deliver skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive network of skill 
development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. under various schemes, 
viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan 
(JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen 
Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the 
country. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped 
with industry relevant skills. 
 
The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on 01.07.2020 
for formalizing enterprises, expanding access to government support and 
strengthening the MSME ecosystem. A total of 8.9 crore Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have been registered on Udyam Registration 
Portal, including Udyam Assist Platform (UAP), providing employment to over 
39 crore people across the country. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has initiated 
‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of IT Manpower for 
Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence. 
 
Also, the Government is implementing Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) 
Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana to support 
employment generation, enhance employability and social security across all 
sectors, with special focus on the manufacturing sector. The scheme with an 
outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 
Crore jobs in the country, over a period of 2 years.  
 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, is 
running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop solution 
for providing career related services including jobs from private and 
government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job search & 
matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill 
development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a digital platform 
[www.ncs.gov.in]. 
 
*****

entries.t: Harassment of Women Research Scholars in Universities
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2519 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
HARASSMENT OF WOMEN RESEARCH SCHOLARS IN UNIVERSITIES 
 
2519 Sh. Giridhari Yadav:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing incidents of mental, physical and 
sexual exploitation/harassment of research scholars, particularly women research scholars, by 
their guides/supervisors and others in Government and Private Universities; 
(b) if so, the impact of these incidents on women research scholars and the major reasons 
behind them; 
(c) the status of Internal Complaints Committees (ICC) under the UGC (Prevention, 
Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment of Women Employees and Students in 
Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2015 and the POSH Act, 2013, including the 
number of complaints received and disposed off; 
(d) whether the Government proposes any additional measures to prevent exploitation of 
research scholars, such as mentoring guidelines, digital complaint portals, stricter penalties 
and special safeguards for women, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the time by which these measures are likely to be implemented? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c) The Government is committed to ensuring a safe, secure and gender-sensitive 
environment in all Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs). In compliance with the Sexual 
Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, 
UGC has notified UGC (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment of 
Women Employees and Students in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2015, 
which, being statutory in nature, are binding on Universities and Colleges. The said 
Regulations apply to all Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) across the country.  The UGC 
Regulations decisively oppose all forms of sexual harassment against women employees and 
students of all sexes in HEIs, and provide the mechanism of prevention, prohibition, and 
redressal of sexual harassment of women employees and students, including research 
scholars. "Student" means a person duly admitted and pursuing a programme of study either 

 
 
through regular mode or distance mode. Consequently, research scholars are already covered 
under the existing regulatory framework.  
 
According to the UGC Regulations, 2015, every HEI is mandated to constitute an Internal 
Complaints Committee (ICC) for receiving and inquiring into complaints of sexual 
harassment and prescribes detailed procedures for filing, inquiry and disposal of complaints 
in a time-bound manner. According to this framework, the respective HEIs conduct the 
awareness and gender sensitisation programmes, submit their Annual Returns on complaints 
of sexual harassment in compliance with UGC Regulation, 2015. As per the available 
information, all the UGC-funded Central Universities have constituted Internal Complaints 
Committee in accordance with UGC Regulations.  
 
(d) & (e) UGC has also undertaken various initiatives to ensure strict compliance with the 
mandates related to the constitution and functioning of Internal Complaints Committees 
(ICCs) in all Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs). The key initiatives are as follows: - 
 
(i) SAKSHAM Portal: Developed to empower women by providing support and 
information on redressal mechanisms, and promoting gender justice and equality.  
 
(ii) Issue of periodical advisory to all HEIs regarding: 
 
 Constitution of ICCs and Special Women's Cells 
 Display of banners and posters 
 Display of names and contact details of ICC members 
 Installation of billboards highlighting penal consequences and women helpline 
numbers  
Additionally, institutions are requested to submit an annual return on cases of sexual 
harassment and complete the online Gender Audit compliance through the SAKSHAM 
Portal.

Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the guidelines titled “Basic Facilities and Amenities for a Safe,

entries.t: Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and Tourism Infrastructure Development
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2520 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
SWADESH DARSHAN 2.0 AND 
 TOURISM INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT 
 
2520. SMT. BIJULI KALITA MEDHI: 
 SMT. D K ARUNA: 
 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the objectives and key features of Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme along 
with projects sanctioned and completed; 
(b) the details of steps taken for development of tourism infrastructure, 
including airports, last -mile connectivity and sustainable tourism 
practices in the country particularly in Telangana; and 
(c) the impact of these initiatives on employment generation, local 
economy and overall growth of the tourism sector in the country 
particularly in Telangana?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM  (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (c): The Ministry of Tourism has revamped the Swadesh Darshan 
scheme as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0) with the objective to develop 
sustainable and responsible tourism destinations in the country, following a 
destination and tourist centric approach. The scheme r ecognizes that 
sustainable and responsible tourism is the key and encourages adoption of 
principles of sustainable tourism including environmental, socio -cultural and 
economic sustainability.  
 
Key feature of Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme includes development of 
tourism experiences and amenities in the country, robust operation and 
management of tourism assets created through the scheme, resulting in 

employment generation and contribution to growth of tourism -related 
businesses etc.  
 
Details of the projects sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 including 
in the State of Telangana is Annexed. All the projects sanctioned under SD2.0 
are at various stages of implementation. 
 
Effective and adequate connectivity is one of the important aspects of 
development of a tourist destination. Ministry of Tourism works closely with 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Ministry of Civil Aviation and other 
line Ministries to ensure impr oved connectivity including airports, last mile 
connectivity etc. to tourist destinations. 
 
Ministry of Tourism, in collaboration with Ministry of Civil Aviation under 
their Regional Connectivity Scheme - Ude Desh Ka Aam Naagrik  (RCS-UDAN) 
has identified 53 tourism routes in the country including in the state of 
Talangana for better air connectivity. 
 
During the last seven years after commencement of the scheme, 637 RCS 
routes connecting 92 unserved and underserved airports (including 15 
heliports & 02 water aerodromes) have been operationalised till date. Total 
domestic passengers travelled through RCS -UDAN are more than 154 lakhs 
connecting 3,17,000 RCS flights till date. The Viability Gap Funding (VGF) 
disbursed RACFT to selected Airline Operators (SAOs) is Rs. 4087 Crore. 
 
Inspired by the success, Union Cabinet has approved the Modified 
Regional Connectivity Scheme–UDAN for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36 
with a total outlay of ₹28,840 crore. The Scheme envisages development of 
100 airports from existing unserved airstrips, operational support for regional 
aerodromes, development of 200 modern helipads in hilly, remote, island and 
aspirational regions, and continued Viability Gap Funding (VGF) for regional air 
routes. The Scheme is expected to strengthen regional connectivity, improve 
last-mile access to tourist destinations, particularly in underserved areas, and 
boost tourism, trade and economic development across the country. 
 
Swadesh Darshan Scheme further encourages State Governments/UT 
Administrations including State of Telangana to undertake due consultations 
with local communities and stakeholders, use of renewable energy, eco -
friendly materials, adopt sustainable tourism p ractices, development of 

accessible infrastructure and services, focus on capacity building, local 
entrepreneurship etc. 
 
The scheme envisages to have a significant positive impact on multiple 
facets of tourism development in the country, including Tourism Growth, Boost 
to Local Economies, Infrastructure Creation, Employment Generation and 
Promotion of Tourism.  
 
Further, The Ministry of Tourism has formulated a National Strategy for 
Sustainable Tourism and the following strategic pillars have been identified 
for development of sustainable tourism: 
 
i. Promoting Environmental Sustainability 
ii. Protecting Biodiversity 
iii. Promoting Economic Sustainability 
iv. Promoting Socio-Cultural Sustainability 
v. Scheme for Certification of Sustainable Tourism 
vi. IEC and Capacity Building Governance 
 
The Ministry has also launched the Travel for LiFE initiative to promote 
sustainable tourism across the country and to encourage tourists as well as 
tourism businesses to adopt sustainable practices to preserve local culture, 
environment and heritage. 
 
 
******

entries.t: Assessment of Skill Gap in Tribal Areas
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  2521 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
  
ASSESSMENT OF SKILL GAP IN TRIBAL AREAS 
 
2521 DR. MALLU RAVI: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the effectiveness of standardized skilling 
programmes in Scheduled and tribal areas, including the Nallamala  region of Telangana, 
where many tribal communities possess traditional expertise in forestry, non -timber forest 
produce, livestock, fisheries, medicinal plants and eco -conservation but they are given the 
training that is often unrelated to their livelihood needs; 
 
(b)  whether the Government has conducted any skill -gap and livelihood mapping to align 
training with indigenous knowledge, local resources and seasonal occupations district-wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to introduce region -specific, community -designed 
courses in collaboration with Tribal Research Institutes, Krishi Vigyan Kendras and industry 
under Skill India and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY); 
 
(d)  whether Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and entrepreneurship support is likely to 
be expanded for tribal youth; and 
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof, State and district-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (e):  Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through 
an extensive network of skill development centres / institutes under various sc hemes, viz. 
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Sikhshan Sansthan (JSS), National 
Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including 
scheduled and tribal areas of Nallamala region of Telangana. The SIM aims at enabling youth 
of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.  
 
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana:  MSDE is implementing Pradhan Mantri Kaushal 
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 as a part of Skill India Program for imparting skill development 
training through Short-Term Training (STT), up-skilling and re-skilling through Recoginition of 
Prior Learning (RPL) to the youths across 111 aspirational districts. PMKVY aims to enhance 
the employability of youth within their local regions and thereby reduce distress migration. 
Under PMKVY 4.0, implementation is being decentralized with a focus  on District Skill 
Committees (DSCs) and Skill Hub Institutions to increase last -mile reach, enhance local 
employability and reduce inter -state migration. The scheme adopts targeted measures, 

including Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) for informal workers in remote and tribal border 
areas, enabling them to obtain formal certification and improved livelihood opportunities. 
 
Under PMKVY, as on 30.06.2026, a total of 58,510 beneficiaries have been trained/oriented in 
the Nallamala region of Telangana in various sectors. 
 
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission:  The Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the 
scheme Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya  Vikas Mission (PMJVM) through Tribal Co -operative 
Marketing Development Federation (TRIFED) to facilitate and promote livelihood opportunities 
and entrepreneurship for the tribal population by facilitating the value addition, branding, and 
marketing of Minor Forest Produces and local agricultural goods. TRIFED has sanctioned 4172 
Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVKs) under the scheme, associating 12,48,067 members across 
the country.  
 
Tribal Research Institutes:  The Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs), functioning as the state -
level research arms of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, serve as knowledge and research hubs for 
tribal development, preservation of tribal cultural heritage, evidence -based planning and 
legislation, capacity building of tribal communities and associated institutions, and 
dissemination of information and awareness. These institutes, supported by the Ministry of 
Tribal Affairs, work alongside national initiatives to strengthen tribal welfare and development. 
 
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati 
Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyaan (PMJANMAN) : The Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh 
Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyaan (PMJANMAN) 
are flagship missions of the Government of India dedicated to holistic development and benefit 
saturation across tribal regions. DAJGUA envisions the comprehensive development of tribal 
areas and communities by addressing critical gaps in infrastructure, healthcare, education, and 
livelihoods through 25 interventions coordinated across 17 Minist

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 2522 
ANSWERED ON- 03/08/2026 
CONTINUATION OF SAMAGRA SHIKSHA SCHEME 
 
†2522. Shri Harish Chandra Meena: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has approved the continuation of the Samagra Shiksha Scheme beyond 
31 March 2026 and the revised period of implementation, outlay and Central share for the 16th 
Finance Commission cycle, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the budget approved for Rajasthan for the financial year 2025 -26, along with the percentage of 
the Central share released and utilised; 
(c) the number of PM SHRI schools selected and operational in Rajasthan, including Tonk and 
Sawai Madhopur as on 31 March 2026; and 
(d) the number of out-of-school children identified in the survey conducted during the financial year 
2024-25 along with the gender-wise details of Tonk and Sawai Madhopur? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): Samagra Shiksha Scheme approved for the XVth Finance Commission cycle ended on  31st 
March, 2026.    However, Ministry of Finance has granted an interim extension for continuation of 
the Scheme from 1st April, 2026 to 30th September, 2026.  The Budgetary Estimates of the Samagra 
Shiksha Scheme for the period 2026 -27 is ₹ 4 2,100/- crore.  The Scheme is to be appraised and 
approved by the competent authority for continuation beyond 31st March, 2026. 
(b): Under Samagra Shiksha Scheme, annual plans are prepared by the respective State/UT as 
per their requirement and priorities.  These annual plans are appraised and approved by the Project 
Approval Board in the Department in consultation with the respective State/UT, as per the 
programmatic and financial norms of the Scheme. 
 Accordingly, central share of ₹ 3,705.07 crore was approved and ₹ 2,982.26 crore (80.49%) 
was released to the State of Rajasthan for the period 2025 -26.  An expenditure (including state 
share) of ₹  4,486.87 crore has been reported by the State on the PRABANDH portal of this  
Department.   

(c): Under PM SHRI Scheme, a total of 749 schools including 100 Central Government schools 
(64 Kendriya Vidyalayas, 35 Navodaya Vidyalayas and 1 NCERT) have been selected  and are 
operational as PM SHRI schools from the State of Rajasthan. Of  these, 19 schools including 3 
Central Government schools (2 Kendriya Vidyalayas and 1 Navodaya Vidyalaya) from Tonk 
district and 13 schools including 3 Central Governm ent school (2 Kendriya Vidyalayas and 1 
Navodaya Vidyalaya) from Sawai Madhopur have been selected  and are operational  under PM 
SHRI Scheme. 
(d): As per the information uploaded/provided by the State on the PRABANDH portal (2024-25) 
of the Department, 1031 1 children (5297 boys, 5012 girls and 2 transgender children) have been 
identified as Out of School Children (OoSC).  Out of these , 85 children (43 boys and 42 girls) and 
281 children (158 boys and 123 girls) have been identified as OoSC by the State in th e Tonk and 
Sawai Madhopur district, respectively.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2523 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
RECOGNITION OF PRIOR LEARNING CERTIFICATE 
  
2523.  SMT. BHARTI PARDHI: 
           SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR: 
           SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE: 
           SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE: 
           DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)     the short-term training targets set under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 for 
financial year 2025-26 and 2026-27 particularly in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; 
 
(b)     the number of Recognition of Prior Learning certifications issued to informal workers; 
 
(c)     the new industry-aligned job roles introduced covering emerging sectors like AI, drones 
and renewables; 
 
(d)     the school-to-skill convergence programmes linking vocational education with PMKVY; 
and 
 
(e)     whether PMKVY 5.0 Guidelines preparation has commenced , if so, the priority focus 
areas thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a)      Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 is being implemented from FY 
2022–23 through Short -Term Training (STT) and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL). The 
scheme is demand -driven and industry -oriented; therefore, no state -wise training targets, 
including for Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, have been set under PMKVY 4.0.  
  
(b)      As on 30.06.2026, under PMKVY 4.0, a total of 3,32,137 candidates were certified under 
Recognition of Prior Learning across the country.  
  
(c)      National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) regulated ecosystem 
offers NSQF -aligned and NSQC -approved Qualifications, National Occupational Standards 
(NOSs) and Micro -Credentials in a range of emerging technology domains. At present, 116  
courses related to Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, 54 courses related to 
Automation and Robotic Processing, 80 courses related to Data Analytics, 71 courses related 
to Cyber Security, 17 courses related to Drone Technology, and 99 courses re lated to Green 
Skills are available, enabling learners to acquire industry -relevant competencies aligned with 
evolving technological advancements and workforce requirements. Further, under SOAR 
program, 50 AI and AI application -oriented courses focused on AI for jobs, workplace 
productivity, sector-specific applications, inclusivity, and contextualized AI applications for the 

unorganized sector are added. These courses span sectors such as Healthcare, 
Manufacturing, Logistics, Beauty & Wellness, Furniture & Fittings, Handicrafts, Electronics, 
Information Technology and Capital Goods.  
  
(d)  In line with the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to integrate vocational 
education with mainstream education, PMKVY supports skill development among school and 
college dropouts, out-of-school children, and unemployed youth in the 15–45 years age group. 
The scheme has been implemented in coordination with the Department of School Education 
and Literacy (DoSEL ) and provides demand -driven, industry -linked skilling opportunities 
aligned with learners’ aspirations and employment needs. Further, school infrastructure has 
been leveraged as Skill Hubs beyond regular school hours and on non-working days to expand 
access to vocational education and training.  
 
In addition, the MSDE has implemented the project “Establishment of Skill Labs and Training 
of Trainers in 400 Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) and 200 Eklavya  Model Residential 
Schools (EMRSs) for Delivery of Skilling Courses”, funded through National Skill Development 
Fund (NSDF). The EMRSs established by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, provide quality 
residential education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students, pa rticularly those residing in remote 
and tribal areas. The project aimed to strengthen the reach of vocational education in schools 
through the establishment of 1,200 vocational skill labs aligned with the CBSE curriculum 
across selected JNVs and EMRSs, wit h two skill labs in each school. To ensure the effective 
delivery of vocational education, the project also included a capacity -building component for 
1,200 skill teachers, with two teachers trained per school.  
  
(e)      The PMKVY 4.0 scheme is extended for two years beyond 31.3.2026.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2525 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 03 AUGUST 2026 / SHRAVANA 12, 1948 (SAKA) 
Implementation of PMJDY in Cachar District of Assam 
2525. SHRI PARIMAL SUKLABAIDYA: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of Pradhan  Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts opened in  Assam, 
including district-wise details with special reference to Cachar district and the number of women 
account holders; 
(b) the details of banking facilities, RuPay debit cards, overdraft,  insurance and Direct Benefit  
Transfer (DBT) benefits provided to PMJDY account holders in Cachar district; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any assess ment of  unbanked households,  dormant 
accounts and financial literacy in Cachar district, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken to expand banking access in remote, tea garden, flood -prone and rural areas of 
Cachar district through Banking Cor respondents, digital banking and financial inclusion  
initiatives, along with clarification on the applicability of minimum balance requirements for  
PMJDY accounts?  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d) District wise total number of accounts opened under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana 
(PMJDY) alongwith the number of female beneficiaries, in the State of Assam is at Annexure-I. 
Out of the total of 12,16,176 PMJDY accounts in the District of Cachar 8,57,203 are operative, as on 
15.07.2026. Further, total 7,92,456 RuPay debit cards  for PMJDY accounts have been issued in 
Cachar District. 
Additionally, social security coverage in Cachar district, including PMJDY account holders , 
comprises of 6.97 lakh Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) enrolments and 3.20 lakh 
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) enrolments. 
The data regarding the number of PMJDY accounts linked to DBT Schemes and the district -wise 
PMJDY Overdraft is not c entrally maintained. However, PMJDY guidelines envisage channeling 
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) from the Government to the beneficiaries’ Jan -Dhan accounts. 
Beneficiaries of different Government schemes are being given benefits directly in their bank 
accounts, including PMJDY accounts. 
To ensure accessibility of banking services in rural and remote areas, the endeavour of the 
Government is to provide a banking outlet (Bank branch / Business Correspondent / India Post 
Payments Bank) within 5 kilometres of all inhabited villages in the country. Availability of banking 
outlets is monitored by a Geographic Information System (GIS) based App., namely, Jan Dhan 
Darshak (JDD) App. 
As per the JDD App, all inhabited villages in Cachar District of Assam are covered by banking outlet 
within 5 km radius, as on 30.06.2026. 
PMJDY accounts are offered as Zero balance accounts and hence minimum balance is not applicable. 
Moreover, the Centre for Financial Literacy (CFL) Project has been initiated by the Reserve Bank of 
India (RBI) since 2017 with an objective to adopt community -led innovative and participatory 
approaches to financial literacy. A total of 2,421 CFLs have been set up across the country, with one 
CFL covering three blocks on an average.  
Banks regularly organise camps, to create awareness about the various schemes, basic banking, 
digital financial literacy, consumer protection etc.

each of the last five years, insurer-wise; 
(c) the major reasons identified for the increase in premature policy surrenders, including 
financial distress, policy mis-selling, affordability issues and inadequate awareness among 
policyholders; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the rising surrender rate on 
household savings, long-term financial security and the insurance penetration of the country, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to strengthen safeguards relating to policy sales, 
disclosure norms, free -look provisions and surrender value regulations to protect 
policyholders, if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)  the steps taken by the Government and the insurance regulator to reduce policy lapses 
and premature surrenders, improve grievance redressal and enhance financial literacy 
among insurance consumers? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE  
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to ( b): Surrender and withdrawals as a share of the total benefits paid by life insurers 
have increased from 32 per cent in FY 2021-22 to 39 per cent in FY 2025-26, indicating an 
increase in surrender and withdrawal behaviour over the last five years.  Also, surrender & 
withdrawal as a proportion of total benefits has overtaken the maturity benefits paid by life 
insurance sector.    The proportion of maturity benefits in total benefits paid by life insurers 
has decreased from 48% in FY2021-22 to 37% in the FY2025-26.

protection and the overall stability of the insurance sector.   Based on such monitoring, 
appropriate supervisory and regulatory measures are undertaken, wherever considered 
necessary, to strengthen policyholder protection, improve product design and disclosures, 
promote sound risk management, governance practices and policyholders’ awareness.

DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM CORRIDORS IN TELANGANA 
 
2527. SHRI MADHAVANENI RAGHUNANDAN RAO: 
 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to develop tourism corridors 
in the State of Telangana by connecting ancient temples, heritage 
monuments and other historical sites and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of such tourism corridor projects proposed, sanctioned or 
under implementation in Telangana, along with their present status; 
(c) whether Government has received any proposals from the State 
Government of Telangana for the development of such tourism corridors 
or heritage tourism projects and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of financial assistance sanctioned or proposed by the 
Government for the development of heritage tourism infrastructure in 
Telangana during the last five years? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM  (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)

and tourism products including tourism corridors is primarily undertaken by

efforts of  tourism infrastructure development by extending financial 
assistance to the State Governments /UT Administrations. 
 

In addition, Government of India under its initiative for ‘Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic 
Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ scheme, has also provided financial 
assistance to the States including Telangana  in the year 2024 -25 for 
development of tourism projects. 
 
Receiving/ submission of proposal/ Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) from 
the SGs/UTAs is a continuous process and projects are sanctioned subject to 
adherence to scheme guidelines, availability of funds, Government directions, 
inter-se priority etc.

entries.t: Filling up of Board-level positions in CPSEs
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC ENTERPRISES 
*****  
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2528 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 3rd AUGUST, 2026 
 
Filling up of Board-level positions in CPSEs 
 
2528. Shri Kali Charan Singh:                  
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of sanctioned and filled posts of Chairperson, Chairman and Managing 
Director (CMD), Managing Director, Functional Directors and Independent 
Directors as on 30 June 2026, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSE)-wise; 
(b) the number of Board -level positions lying vacant for more than six months and 
more than one year, respectively; 
(c) whether meetings of the Boards, Audit Committees, CSR Committees and other 
statutory committees have been affected due to shortage of Independent 
Directors, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has fixed any timeline for completion of appointments 
through the appropriate selection process, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken to  ensure that prolonged vacancies do not adversely affect 
governance, investment decisions, project execution and the financial 
performance of CPSEs? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) and (b) : Public Enterprises Selection Board (PESB) is responsible for the 
selection and  recommendation of personnel to the posts of Chairman/CMD/MD 
(Level-I) and Functional Director (Level -II) in the CPSEs. The Government however, 
in some instances, may decide to fill a particular Board l evel post through modes 
other than PESB procedure such as Search -cum-Selection Committee (SCSC) 
procedure, on deputation basis, etc. or decide to keep particular Board level post(s) 
in abeyance. 
As per available information from PESB, in case of Board level posts in CPSEs being 
filled through PESB procedure, t here are 22 vacant posts of full -time functional 
Directors (7 posts of CMD/MD and 15 posts of functional Directors) in various 
CPSEs having date of vacancy prior to 30.07.2026. Of these 22 posts, only three 
posts are vacant for more than six months. PESB has already furnished its 
recommendations for other vacant Board level posts having date of vacancy prior to 
30.07.2026 for processing by the c oncerned administrative Ministry for 
approval/decision of the competent authority.  As per available information, presently 
75 positions of non -official (Independent) Directors are filled in various CPSEs as 
against the requirements of around 750 as per provisions of Companies Act, 2013 
and SEBI (LODR) Regulations.  The Search Committee has made recommendations 

 
 
for filling up around more 100 positions of non-official (Independent) Directors on the 
Boards of various CPSEs. 
(c) : The meetings of Board and Board Committees are required to be held as per 
relevant provisions of Companies Act, 2013 and/or SEBI (LODR) Regulations  which 
also inter alia prescribe the constitution of Board Committees. The CPSEs are 
independent Board-driven entities functioning under the administrative jurisdiction of 
the concerned Ministr ies/Departments. The Board of Directors of CPSE and 
concerned administrative Ministry/Department is required to ensure compliance with 
these provisions to ensure smooth functioning of Board and Board Committees.  
(d) and (e) : It has been the constant endeavour of the Government to ensure that 
Board level posts in the CPSEs are filled up as per extant procedure in a timely 
manner. The Government has issued timelines for processing of the proposals for 
appointment and extension/non-extension to Board level post s in CPSEs which inter 
alia provide that the administrative Ministries/Departments are required to initiate the 
job description (JD) for a post and communicate the same to PESB within the 
stipulated time i.e. three months in advance of the stipulated period of one year of 
the date of occurrence of  vacancy. If any Ministry/Department does not  forward the 
JD for a post to PESB within the  stipulated time, PESB initiates the JD one year  
before the occurrence of the vacancy and starts  consultation with the 
Ministry/Department so that  the selection process is started expeditiously.  To track 
the status of both existing and anticipated  vacancies and initiating timely action, 
PESB has developed a comprehensive  vacancy tracking  dashboard reflecting 
various milestones such as creation of vacancy, initiation of job description, 
advertising the post, screening/shortlisting the applications and convening the 
selection meetings. 
The Government has also issued guidelines regarding assignment of additional 
charge for manning vacant Board level posts in CPSEs so that regular functioning of 
CPSEs is not adversely affected. 
 
 
*****

MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA

†2529. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that requisite tourism 
infrastructure is lacking at the historically and mythologically 
important Mahatma Vidur Kutir in Bijnor district, despite the

(c)  whether the Government is considering any special project or 
scheme to develop Mahatma Vidur Kutir as a major spiritual and 
heritage tourism destination; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and the proposed timeline therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM         (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): Identification and development of tourism infrastructure, 
amenities and experiences at tourist destinations including places of 
historical, cultural and religious significance such as Mahatma Vidur Kutir 
in Bijnor district is primarily undertaken by the co ncerned State 
Government/UT Administration. However, the Ministry of Tourism, under 
its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh Darshan 2.0 
(SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD), and 
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Her itage Augmentation Drive 
(PRASHAD), provides financial assistance for the development of tourism 
related infrastructure and experiences across the country, including 
those in the State of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
At present, no proposal specific to the development of Mahatma 
Vidur Kutir in Bijnor district is under consideration in the Ministry.  

 
However, receiving proposals for tourism infrastructure 
development is a continuous process. The Proposals for seeking financial 
assistance for the development of the tourism infrastructure are 
formulated by the concerned States and UTs. The proposals received are 
examined in accordance with the prescribed guidelines, and financial 
assistance is provided subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions 
and availability of funds. 
 
The details of projects sanctioned under the aforementioned 
schemes in the State of Uttar Pradesh, is given in the Annexure.

entries.t: Setting up of state-of-the-art Software Park in Dhanbad
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2530 
ANSWERED ON 03/08/2026 
 
Setting up of state-of-the-art Software Park in Dhanbad 
 
†2530.  Shri Dulu Mahato: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that Dhanbad has prestigious institutes like Indian 
Institute of Technology (IIT-ISM), BIT Sindri and Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research 
(CSIR-CIMFR), from where thousands of technically skilled youth pass out every year, if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) whether these talented youths have to migrate to metropolitan cities like Bengaluru, Pune 
and Noida for employment due to lack of Information Technology (IT)/Software industry in 
Dhanbad, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to set up a state -of-the-art software park or 'Industry-
Academia Innovation Centre' in Dhanbad in coordination with the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology under the National Education Policy; and 
(d) if so, the steps being taken by the Government in this direction to provide employment to 
local youth, foster startup culture and prevent brain drain? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
(a) to (d):  In the state of Jharkhand, the Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines), 
Dhanbad [IIT (ISM) Dhanbad], originally established in 1926 as the Indian School of Mines, was 
accorded IIT status in 2016 through an Act of Parliament and is recognized as an  Institution of 
National Importance (INI). Further, other INIs including National Institute of Technology (NIT) 
Jamshedpur and I ndian Institute of Information Technology (I IIT) Ranchi have also been 
functioning in the state of Jharkhand. These institutes are known for their excellence in technical 

education, advanced research in both fundamental and applied domains, innovation, promotion 
of entrepreneurship, and consultancy services to industry. 
A significant number of alumni of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad are presently serving in reputed 
Central Public Sector Undertakings, State Government undertakings, and leading private sector 
organisations located across the country including in Dhanbad and other parts of Jharkhand. IIT 
(ISM), Dhanbad, through its incubation centres, has supported the incubation of 
approximately 150 startups, facilitating access to funding from various venture capital firms and 
government agencies. In addition, the Institute conducts  Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY) training programmes for local youth and faculty members from other institutions 
(Training of Trainers).  
 
At present, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad operates  four innovation and incubation centres  with 
support from various Ministries and Government agencies. The Institute has established a robust 
innovation ecosystem through its four incubation centres —Technology Innovatio n in 
Exploration & Mining Foundation (TexMin Foundation), CIIE IIT (ISM) Dhanbad Foundation, 
Atal Community Innovation Centre  (ACIC IIT( ISM) Dhanbad) , and the CIL Innovation 
&  Incubation Centre. These centres promote innovation, entrepreneurship, startu p incubation, 
industry–academia collaboration, technology commercialization, and skill development.  
 
The Birsa Institute of Technology, Sindri, is under the administrative control of the 
Government of Jharkhand. It currently offers Bachelor of Technology programmes in varied 
engineering disciplines. CSIR-Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research (CSIR -CIMFR), 
Dhanbad, a constituent laboratory of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), 
undertakes R&D activities across the entire coal -energy value chain, covering exploration, 
mining, and utilization. 
Software Technology Parks of India (STPI)  under the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology (MeitY)  has established its centre at Dhanbad (Jharkhand).  STPI 
Dhanbad has been developed with state-of-the-art IT grade infrastructure at BIT Sindri Campus, 
Dhanbad (Jharkhand). The centre provides services to IT/ITeS industry & startups/entrepreneurs 
of the region by offering Statutory services, Incubation services, High Speed Data 
Communication (HSDC) services, cyber security services, project management & consultancy 
services, IT managed services/co-location services and startup promotion services. 
*********

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2531 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 4th AUGUST 2026 
 
‘Establishment of PACS’ 
 
2531.    Shri Zia Ur Rehman:  
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has taken steps to strengthen Primary Agricultural Credit Societies 
(PACS), if so, the details thereof; and  
(b) whether new PACS have been established during the last three years State-wise and if so, the 
details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a): The Ministry of Cooperation has adopted a "Whole -of-Government" approach to strengthen 
Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) as vibrant, transparent and economically sustainable 
grassroots institutions by converging schemes and services of various Ministries/Departments at the 
PACS level. Towards this objective, following initiatives have been undertaken: 
(i)  Computerization of PACS 
To strengthen Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), the Government launched the Central 
Sector Project for Computerization of PACS in 2022. Under the project, functional PACS are being 
brought onto a common Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)-based national software platform and 
linked with the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) through State 
Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), with the objective 
of improving operational efficiency, transparency, accountability, and ease of doing business in the 
cooperative sector.  
(ii) Decentralised Grain Storage Programme 
The Government approved the Decentralized Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector on 31 May 
2023 to strengthen agricultural infrastructure at the PACS level. The programme envisages creation 
of decentralized storage infrastructure, including warehouses, custom hiring centres, primary 

Page 2 of 3 
 
processing units and Fair Price Shops, through convergence of existing Government schemes such 
as: 
• Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF);  
• Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI);  
• Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM); and  
• Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME). 
(iii) Business Diversification of PACS by enabling them to function as Multipurpose 
Institutions 
Model Bye -laws have been formulated and circulated to all States/UTs to enable Primary 
Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to diversify into more than 25 economic activities, including 
dairy, fisheries, floriculture, food grain procurement, warehousing, f ertilizer and seed distribution, 
custom hiring centres, LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorships, Fair Price Shops and other farmer-
centric activities. 
After adoption of the Model Bye -laws, PACS have also been enabled to undertake the following 
activities: 
• Common Service Centres (CSCs):  PACS have been enabled to provide more than 300 
citizen-centric digital services, including banking, insurance, Aadhaar enrolment/updation 
and other e-Governance services.  
• Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras (PMKSKs):  PACS have been upgraded as 
PMKSKs for providing fertilizers, pesticides and other agricultural inputs under one roof.  
• Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs):  PACS have been made 
operational as PMBJKs for providing quality generic medicines at affordable prices in rural 
areas.  
• Retail Petrol/Diesel Outlets:  PACS have been accorded priority under Combined 
Category-2 (CC-2) for allotment of retail outlets.  
 
(b) The State -wise details of new PACS established during last three years is enclosed at 
Annexure.

October 2021, is a transformative approach for planning and development of

infrastructure projects such as schools, hospital, anganwadis etc. As on date,

on PMGS-NMP. The State of Telangana is also a part of this initiative and using

projects including those in Warangal district.

been integrated with PMGS-NMP - Warangal district has no aspirational block 
as on date. 
The Network Planning Group (NPG), constituted under the PM GatiShakti 
National Master Plan (PMGS -NMP) framework, evaluates the critical 
infrastructure projects of the central Government to ensure integrated planning, 
multi-modality, inter-modality, synchronization of eﬀorts, last mile connectivity, 
comprehensive development in and around the project location, data driven 
decision makings, etc at the planning stage. As on date, 23 projects falling fully 
or partially in the State of Telangana ha ve been evaluated by NPG which 
benefits connectivity to Warangal district and one of these, i.e. a road project 
related to Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is passing through 
Warangal district. 
Further, 03 Rail connectivity projects of about 447 km,  costing about ₹ 7843 
Crore and 04 National Highway projects of about 185 km, costing about ₹6,133 
Crore have been sanctioned to improve the connectivity in Warangal district. 
Moreover, Under the PM MITRA Scheme, a Brownfield Textile Park has been 
inaugurated at Warangal over 1,327 acres with a project cost of about ₹1,696  
crore.

respective infrastructure projects, including social infrastructure projects, 
in integrated, synchronized and coordinated manner to provide seamless 
and efficient connectivity for the movement of people, goods, and services 
across various modes of transport, thereby enhancing last -mile 
connectivity and reducing travel time. PMGS NMP is also helping in 
improvement in ease of doing business  through better site selection, 
reduced delays, and enhanced transparency. 
 PM MITRA Park oﬀers excellent multimodal connectivity to major railway

bureaucratic framework in  Chandigarh to ensure administrative efficiency

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO– 2534 
 ANSWERED ON- 04.08.2026 
  
WOMEN REPRESENTATIVES IN PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS 
  
†2534. SHRI PATEL UMESHBHAI BABUBHAI: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government is aware that the tenure of the woman Chairperson in District 
Panchayats of Daman and Diu has been fixed to approximately two years and six months 
instead of complete five years if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the date on which this rule was implemented and through which notification or 
amendment it was made effective along with the rationale of the Government behind it; 
(c) whether this system prevents women representatives from completing their full tenure, 
which creates obstacles in the development of their leadership, decision-making capacity and 
administrative experience; 
(d) whether this provision is contrary to the principle of equality enshrined in Article 14 of 
the Constitution and the spirit of political empowerment of women and should be considered 
an injustice to women; and 
(e) if so, the steps being taken to repeal/amend this provision, and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
  
  
  
 ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) and (b)        Yes, Sir. The Union Territory (UT) Administration has informed that ‘The Dadra 
and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Panchayat Regulation, 2012’ was amended vide 
Presidential Regulation Order, 2020 dated 8th October, 2020 and notified in the Official Gazette 
on 17.04.2021, whereby the tenure of the Chairperson in District Panchayats, which includes 
women Chairperson has been fixed to two years and six months from the date they are appointed 
for its first meeting and no longer. The office of the Chairperson in District Panchayat shall be 
reserved for women in every second term. The UT Administration has also informed that the 
purpose of this amendment is to promote women empowerment by strengthening their leadership 
role and administrative experience. 

2 
 
 (c)       No, Sir. The UT Administration has informed that the period of two years and six months 
is specifically reserved for women to strengthen their leadership role, decision making capacities 
and administrative experience along with the provision to assume leadership responsibilities for 
the remaining tenure.  
(d)        The UT Administration has informed that the said provision is not contrary to the 
principle of equality enshrined in Article 14 of the Constitution and the spirit of political 
empowerment of women and should not be considered an injustice to women. It is seen as a 
mechanism to fulfill the spirit of political empowerment of women by ensuring that more 
representatives, particularly those from reserved categories and women, have the opportunities to 
hold leadership roles. 
(e)        The UT Administration has informed that in the view of the provisions mentioned in the 
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Panchayat Regulation, 2012, no amendments are 
required.

REVISION OF NCRB DATA  
 
2536.      DR. AMAR SINGH 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of changes made to the National Crime Records Bureau 
(NCRB) data collection formats and reporting templates following the 
transition from the Indian Penal Code, 1860 to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 
2023;  
 
(b) whether the methodology for collection, classification and reporting of 
crime statistics has been revised in view of the implementation of the 
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and if so, the details thereof along with the reasons 
therefor;  
 
(c) the measures adopted by the NCRB to ensure the accuracy, authenticity 
and consistency of crime data received from States and Union Territories; 
and  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to expand the role of the NCRB 
beyond data collection and publication including crime  analytics, policy 
support and research and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) to (c):  NCRB releases three annual statistical reports namely 'Crime in 
India', 'Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India' and 'Prison Statistics India'. 
The publications collate data of a calendar year. Hence, the process of 
collecting data is initiated only after the completion of the respective year. 
The latest published report pertains to the year 2024. 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2536 FOR 04.08.2026 
The data is collected  digitally through a dedicated software application 
developed by the Bureau. The data collection and its 
consolidation/compilation is done at various levels in the District/State by 
the States/UTs and subsequently by the Bureau, through this software 
application. Data submitted by States/Union Territories is extensively 
verified/validated at various levels/stages through the inbuilt checks in the 
software application. In case of discrepancy/inconsistency in the data, the 
same is referred back to the respect ive State/UT for re -validation. 
Necessary trainings for ensuring uniformity are also imparted to the 
States/Union Territories to collect data as per the detailed proformas. 
Amendments/Rectifications, if any, in the data are updated in the database 
by NCRB. Certificate of either ADG/IG in -charge of the SCRB/CID or a letter 
clearly conveying the approval of DG(P) for the correctness of the data is 
being accepted for inclusion of the data in the CII report. The reports 
published by the Bureau are made publicly  available on the website of the 
Bureau. 
The Bureau has updated its data collection formats as per Nyaya Sanhitas 
namely, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha 
Sanhita (BNSS) and collected data pertaining to its implementation from 1st 
July  2024  to  31st  December  2024  in its annual publication Crime in India  
 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2536 FOR 04.08.2026 
 (CII) 2024. The classification of Crime Categories is as per Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita. 
(d): In addition to collection, compilation and publication of crime statistics, 
NCRB is implementing and supporting various policy initiatives of the 
Ministry of Home Affairs, including the Inter -operable Criminal Justice 
System (ICJS), National Automated Fingerprint Identification System 
(NAFIS), Criminal Procedure Identification System (CrPIS), Emergency 
Response Support System (ERSS) and related applications, which facilitate 
use of crime and criminal justice databases for investigation, inter -
operability, data-driven decision-making, and policy formulation.

WHEAT MONOCULTURE AND SOIL DEGRADATION 
 
2538.  SMT. HARSIMRAT KAUR BADAL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृषि और ककसान कल्याण 
मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that Punjab's decades -old rice wheat monoculture 
cycle has severely degraded soil health, reducing organic carbon levels, compacting soil, and 
lowering water holding capacity, as confirmed by a 2026 long-term study by Punjab agricultural 
scientists; 
(b)  the current area under alternative crops (maize, basmati, pulses, oilseeds, fruits, and  
vegetables) in Punjab compared to the rice-wheat coverage, and the year-on-year change since 
2022; 
(c) whether the existing crop diversification incentive of Rs.17,500 per acre for alternative  
crops is being fully paid to farmers in Punjab, and if any delays or shortfalls in payment have  
been reported; and 
(d) the specific measures being taken to restore soil health in Punjab, including promotion 
of green manuring, leguminous cover crops, zero -tillage, and micro -irrigation and the funds  
allocated for this purpose under the National and State budgets? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृषि और ककसान कल्याण राज्य मंत्री (SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a): Yes. As per the long-term study conducted by Punjab Agricultural University, continuous 
rice–wheat monoculture has often been associated with concerns regarding soil degradation 
due to repeated puddling, intensive tillage, devoid of legumes or green manuri ng and 
monocropping. Puddling during transplanted rice disrupt soil aggregation, reduce porosity, and 
increase sub -surface compaction, which adversely affect soil physical health without 
appropriate management practices.  However, these effects are largely  reversible through 
scientifically recommended package of practices such as inclusion of legumes, crop rotation, 
balanced fertilizer application, integrated nutrient management, addition of organic manure and 
residue incorporation. 
 

2 
 
 
 
 
(b): The rice and wheat continue to dominate Punjab's agricultural landscape. Rice area in 
Punjab has shown a steady increase from 2,969 thousand hectares in 2021 –22 to 3,268 
thousand hectares in 2025 –26, whereas wheat area has remained largely stable from 3,52 5 
thousand hectares to 3,458.6 thousand hectares during the same period. Over the same period, 
the area under other field crops (maize, pulses and oilseeds) relative to the rice–wheat system 
declined from 8.6% to 6.2%, whereas the share of horticultural cr ops (fruits and vegetables) 
increased gradually from 6.3% to 7.2%, indicating a marginal shift towards horticultural 
diversification while the rice –wheat system continues to predominate.  Crop-wise year-on-year 
area details are given in Annexures I and II. 
 
 
(c): The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DoAFW, GOI) is implementing the 
Crop Diversification Programme (CDP) with aim to demonstrate and promote improved 
production technologies of alternate crops for diversion of paddy cultivation as well as to restore 
soil fertility through cultivation of leguminous crops in the Original Green Revolution States viz; 
Haryana, Punjab & Uttar Pradesh since 2013-14. An amount of Rs. 13.52 crores is allocated to 
the state of Punjab during the financial year 2026 -27 to promote crop diversification in 
convergence mode. Government of Punjab has fully paid Rs.10,000 per ha for Kharif Maize as 
per issued guidelines of CDP scheme. 
 
(d): The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Government of India, is 
implementing various schemes in Punjab, namely PM -PRANAM, National Mission on Natural 
Farming (NMNF), Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme, Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) 
and Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), for restoring soil health and promoting green manuring, 
leguminous cover crops, zero-tillage and micro-irrigation. 
 
 Complementing these initiatives, ICAR is undertaking research through the AICRP on 
Soil Test Crop Response (STCR), Long -Term Fertilizer Experiments (LTFEs), Micro and 
Secondary Nutrients, Agroforestry, Integrated Farming Systems (IFS), Irrigation Water 
Management, and the Network Project on Natural Farming (NPNF). Based on scientific 
evidence generated from these programmes, ICAR promotes soil test -based balanced 
fertilization, Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), green manuring, leguminous cover crops, 
conservation agriculture, zero -tillage and micro -irrigation. ICAR has also developed organic 
production packages for seven cropping systems, including basmati rice–wheat–sunhemp and 
kharif greengram–wheat–summer greengram, and identified maize (cobs/fodder)–potato–onion 
and baby corn –potato–okra as profitable alternativ

practice Natural Farming, to train other farmers, upkeep of livestock, preparation of natural

Organic farming is being promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)

†2541.     SHRI ANOOP PRADHAN VALMIKI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the severe heatwave conditions in 
many parts of the  country and the resulting loss of lives and health crises 
caused by it and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government is considering to declare heatwaves as a 
'natural disaster' under the 'National Disaster Management Act' so that relief 
and rehabilitation schemes can get a legal  framework and if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(c) whether there is any plan to introduce a policy proposal in this direction 
in the near future; and 
 
(d) whether any technical or financial assistance has been provided by the 
Government to the State Governments for the implementation of their Heat 
Action Plans and if so, the details thereof, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a): The Government is aware of the occurrence of heatwave conditions in 
various parts of the country and the associated health impacts. The Ministry 
of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), through the National Programme on 
Climate Change & Human Health (NPCCHH) , implements heat -health 
interventions in accordance with the National Action Plan on Heat Related 
Illness (NAPHRI). 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2541 FOR 04.08.2026 
 
Under this framework, MoHFW has issued Heat Advisories for State Health 
Departments and Public Health Advisories on Extreme Heat/Heatwave , 
along with the seasonal outlook issued by the India Meteorological 
Department (IMD). Based on the IMD Heatwave Warning Bulletin , NPCCHH 
disseminates customised colour -coded health advisories to all States and 
Districts for timely preparedness and response. 
 
National Heat-Related Illness and Death Surveillance (NHRIDS) activated for 
more than 51000 reporting units across the country from all PHCs and above 
hospitals. The total heat stroke cases and deaths due to heat stroke in this 
year till 26th July 2026, are mentioned in Annexure. 
 
(b) and (c):     The 16th Finance Commission, in its recommendations for the 
award period 2026-31, recommended inclusion of heatwaves and lightning  
in the list of notified natural calamities, considering the increasing 
frequency a nd intensity of extreme weather events arising from climate 
change. 
 
Based on these recommendations, the Ministry of Home Affairs has included 
heatwaves and lightning in the list of notified natural calamities under the 
Operational Guidelines for Administr ation of the State Disaster Response 
Fund (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) for the award

period 2026 -31. Accordingly, a policy framework for providing relief 
assistance through SDRF/ NDRF is now in place. Heat Wave Mitigation 
Projects are eligible under the Disaster Mitigation Funds. 
 
(d): The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)  has issued 
National Guidelines for the Effective Management of Heatwaves  and also 
formulated the National Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan – 
Prevention and Management of Heat Wave  in October, 2019 . These 
guidelines facilitate heatwave -prone States and Union Territo ries in 
preparing Heat Action Plans (HAPs).

Initiative to Generate Sustainable Rural Employment 
2543. Shri Dharambir Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any initiative to generate sustainable rural employment 
through watershed development, afforestation, soil conservation and restoration of common lands, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether scientific planning and satellite-based monitoring have been integrated for implementation 
of such projects, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the measures taken to improve long-term livelihood opportunities through natural resource 
management initiatives; and 
(d) whether such projects are proposed to be undertaken in the Bhiwani–Mahendragarh Lok Sabha 
Constituencies, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(Dr. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
 
(a) to (c) :  Watershed Management (WM) Division of Department of Land Resources is implementing 
Watershed Development Component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY).  The 
activities undertaken, inter alia, include ridge area treatment, drainage line treatment, soil and moisture 
conservation, rainwater harvesting, nursery raising, pasture development, livelihoods for asset-less 
persons etc. 
 
Under WDC-PMKSY- 1.0 (for the period 2009-22), DoLR supported implementation of 6382 
projects.  The State-wise details of projects funded by DoLR, projects completed and Central share 
released are given at Annexure-I. Through the implementation of these projects, significant progress has 
been registered. 7.65 lakh water harvesting structures have been created / rejuvenated, 16.41 lakh ha 
additional area has been brought under protective irrigation and 36.34 lakh farmers benefited. In addition 
to this, 1.63 lakh ha have been brought under plantation (Afforestation / Horticulture etc.) and 388.66 
lakh mandays have been generated. The State-wise details of physical achievements under WDC-
PMKSY-1.0 are given at Annexure II. The third party end-line evaluation reports of the completed 
WDC-PMKSY projects have revealed significant improvement in ground water table, increase in 
productivity, vegetative cover, enhanced livelihood opportunities and household incomes in watershed 
project areas. 
  
1 
 

 
The continuation of WDC-PMKSY has been approved by the Government of India on 15.12.2021 as 
‘WDC-PMKSY 2.0’ for the period of 2021-2026 with total outlay of Rs.12404 crore (Central share: Rs. 
8134 crore). Under WDC-PMKSY 2.0, Department has sanctioned 1,220 watershed projects covering 
52.93 Lakh hectares in 28 States and the UTs of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, including Haryana. The 
State-wise details of projects sanctioned, area covered, project cost and Central share released under 
WDC-PMKSY-2.0 are at Annexure III. 
 
The physical achievements made under WDC-PMKSY 2.0, from 2022-23 to 2025-26 include, 1.15 lakh 
WHS (like check dams, anicuts, farm ponds, percolation tanks, trenches etc.) have been created / 
rejuvenated, 2.69 lakh ha have been brought under protective irrigation, 23.29 lakh farmers benefitted 
and 266.05 lakh man days have been generated. The State-wise details of physical achievements under 
WDC-PMKSY-2.0 are given at Annexure IV. 
 
Under the Watershed Development Component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-
PMKSY), several measures have been undertaken to improve long-term livelihood opportunities through 
the restoration and sustainable management of natural resources. These include soil and water 
conservation, groundwater recharge, afforestation, pasture and degraded land development, improved 
production systems and creation of water-harvesting structures. The programme enhances soil moisture, 
promotes groundwater recharge, and expands protective irrigation, thereby supporting climate-resilient 
agriculture, sustainable agricultural practices, crop diversification, integrated farming systems, and 
efficient water use to improve farm productivity. It also promotes livelihood diversification through 
support for livestock, horticulture, fisheries, agroforestry and income-generating activities for landless 
and vulnerable households. In addition, the programme strengthens community institutions through 
capacity-building initiatives and convergence with other rural development programmes for the creation 
of sustainable livelihood assets. These interventions collectively enhance water availability, improve 
agricultural productivity, increase cropping intensity from nil to single crop/single crop to multiple crops 
and generate sustainable employment and long term livelihood opportunities in rural areas.

data and its integration with the Gram Manchitra Application, a spatial planning application

developed by Ministry of Panchayati Raj to help Gram Panchayats in better development

planning at Gram Panchayat level with the use of Geo-spatial Technology. The application 
has tools like road estimate preparation, street light estimation, solar potential assessment etc. 
The high-resolution drone imagery generated under SVAMITVA Scheme are integrated with 
the Gram Manchitra Application which is further used to improve planning of village roads, 
drinking water systems, preparation of village drainage network plans, public utilities, solar 
infrastructure and community assets for an effective Gram Panchayat Development Planning

platforms.  For instance, the Ministry has integrated SVAMITVA datasets with digital

platforms like PM Gati Shakti. Further, States/UTs also strengthen interoperability of 
SVAMITVA datasets with their own platforms such as the interoperability of the 
SVAMITVA datasets with the e-Swathu system of Karnataka.

and 20,364 property cards has been prepared for 230 villages.

SVAMITVA Scheme and Gram Manchitra Application to support evidence-based rural 
planning such as Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP), convergence of Central and 
State Government schemes, infrastructure and asset planning under the PM GatiShakti, 
improved service delivery, and informed decision-making by the Gram Panchayats of 
districts including Kolar district.

within the approved scheme parameters, at prevailing wage rates to

add their own top-up funds to the PMAY-G budget. The State 
government is then responsible for distributing the funds down to

scheme-wise and year-wise;

MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SHRI B. L. VERMA) 
  
(a) and (b): Yes. The Government enacted Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 
2016 which came into force on 19.04.2017. The no. of disabilities has been increased from 7 to 
21. The said Act provides rights and entitlements to Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), which, 
interalia, include right to equality, non-discrimination, protection from cruelty, exploitation, 
right to live with family and community, access to justice, accessibility in voting, legal capacity, 
legal guardianship, health, education, employment, skill development, arts, sports, recreation, 
culture and participation in decision making process. 
  
Section 34 of the said Act provides for 4 % reservation in the government employment to the 
persons with benchmark (40% or above) disabilities. Further, Section 32 of the said Act 
provides 5% reservation in government or government aided higher educational institutions for 
persons with benchmark disabilities. Furthermore, Section 37 of the said Act ensures 5% 
reservation in poverty alleviation and developmental schemes to persons with bench mark 
disabilities.  
 

Though, relief to the disabled is a State subject by virtue of entry 9 of the State List of the 
Constitution of India, the Central Government supplements the efforts of the State 
Governments, regarding educational and employment based support, through its major schemes 
namely Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS),  Assistance to Persons with 
Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP),  Scholarship Schemes and 
Scheme for Implementation of Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 (SIPDA). There 
are no State/ Union Territory-wise budgetary allocations. The schemes are demand driven and 
funds are disbursed as per actual demand.

Approach’ basis wherein claims are worked out on the area of the land parcel based on the

under YES-TECH, vis-à-vis threshold yield, as per the formula in the Operational 
Guidelines of the scheme. In case of no shortfall in yield, no claims become payable.
