SUPPORT FOR FARMER PRODUCER ORGANISATION 
2600. SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M.: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
(a)  whether it is a fact that despite the Government's concerted efforts, many Farmer Producer 
Organisations (FPOs) are struggling to achieve economic viability;  
(b)  whether it is also a fact that the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences has recommended 
that institutional buyers must prioritise (FPOs) in the procurement of both food and non-food 
commodities; 
(c)  whether it is also a fact that the Government has been maintaining that it will help in the 
formation of 10,000 FPOs; 
(d)  whether it is also a fact that many FPOs struggle to achieve the economies of scale required 
for profitability due to many factors; and  
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
 
(a): The Government is implementing the Central Sector Scheme for "Formation and Promotion of 
10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). 10,000 FPOs have been formed under the scheme 
since 2020-21. FPOs undertake a wide range of business activities including agri-input supply, 
aggregation and trading of agricultural produce, value addition and processing, seed production, 
digital commerce through e-market places, custom hiring services & export promotion. From the 
audited financial statements 2024-25 of the scheme FPOs, 6964 FPOs had a turnover of up to 
Rs.50 Lakh, 862 FPOs had a turnover of Rs.50 Lakh to Rs.1 Crore and 1135 FPOs had a turnover 
of over Rs.1 Crore.      
(b): The National Academy of Agricultural Sciences, in Policy Paper No. 144, covers all FPOs 
registered in the country. The recommendations in the Policy Paper No. 144 include promotion of 
FPOs - industry linkages, link institutional buyers with FPOs, strengthening linkage of FPOs with 
Research & Development etc.      
(c): Under the 10K FPO Scheme, financial assistance of up to ₹18 lakh per FPO is provided to 
meet management and handholding expenses during the initial 3 years. A matching Equity Grant 
of up to ₹15 lakh per FPO is  provided to strengthen the capital base of eligible FPOs and Credit 
Guarantee Facility for project loans of up to ₹2 crore per FPO to improve access to institutional 
credit.  In addition, each FPO is provided 5 years of handholding support through a Cluster-Based 
Business Organization (CBBO) for capacity building, business planning, market linkages, and 
overall institutional development.   Till date 827.81 crore has been released to the FPOs registered 
under the 10K FPO Scheme as management cost and Rs.631.98 crore as matching equity grant.  
(d) & (e):  So far, under the 10K FPO Scheme, more than 65 lakh shareholders (predominantly 
small and marginal farmers) have been collectivized to leverage economies of scale.  As on date, 
for greater bargaining for input supply, 6928 FPOs have seed licenses, 4987 have pesticide 
licenses and 6650 have fertilizer licenses.  5765 FPOs have their own processing units and 3083 
FPOs have availed credit guarantee.

(a) to (d): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations 
of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of 
the State Governments and Central Ministries / Departments concerned. 
The Union Budget for  2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to 
keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial 
crops with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of 
production from year 2018-19 onwards. 
  

 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement 
by Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. 
Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India 
(FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. 
Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under 
umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), 
on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when 
market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-
AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd 
(NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton 
and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India 
(CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective 
State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, 
convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage 
and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis 
and depots/godowns are also established at key points. The procurement operation is a 
continuously evolving process and during the last few years, procurement processes 
under MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly 
and linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ procurement portals ensure that 
the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase.  
Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to 
reduce import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses. To encourage 
domestic production of  pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad 
and Masur under the PM-AASHA Scheme on the request of State Government from pre-
registered farmers as much as offered by them through Central Nodal Agencies, namely 
the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and the 
National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF). 
Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component 
under PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which 
are perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS).

2603.  PROF. SOUGATA RAY 
 SHRI KISHORI LAL 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY ¼okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=h½  be 
pleased to state:  
 
  
(a) whether the Government has any policy or legal framework to prohibit the import 
of goods produced wholly or partly through forced labour, including child labour 
and bonded labour, if so, the details thereof;    
(b) whether the Government has examined international practices, including 
import restrictions imposed by other countries on goods suspected to have 
been produced using forced labour; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to introduce legislation, amend the 
Customs Act, or frame rules to prohibit the import of goods manufactured using 
forced labour and to strengthen due diligence in supply chains; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure that India's import policies are 
consistent with its commitments under the Constitution, International Labour 
Organization (ILO) conventions, and international human rights standards 
while safeguarding legitimate trade? 
 
 
ANSWER 
okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=ky; esa jkT;ea=h ¼Jh ftfru izlkn½ 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) Yes. Section 3 of the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 
1992 empowers the Central Government to make provisions for the development 
and regulation of foreign trade by facilitating imports and increasing exports and, in 
particular, to make provision for prohibiting, restricting or otherwise regulating the 
import or export of goods. In exercise of these powers, the Government has inserted 
Paragraph 2.20B in the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023, vide Notification No. 
23/2026-27 dated 13.07.2026, to prohibit the import of goods produced wholly or in 

2 
 
part using forced labour. The Government has also examined international 
practices, including import restrictions imposed by other countries on goods 
suspected to have been produced using forced labour. 
 
"Forced Labour" has been defined under Paragraph 11.64 of the FTP in accordance 
with the ILO Forced Labour Convention, 1930 (No. 29). The Central Government 
may notify specific goods for prohibition under this provision upon completion of due 
enquiry and satisfaction that such goods have been produced wholly or in part using 
forced labour. Bonded labour is addressed under the Bonded Labour System 
(Abolition) Act, 1976, and child labour under the Child and Adolescent Labour 
(Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. 
The Government has also, through Public Notice No. 21/2026-27 dated 13.07.2026, 
inserted Paragraph 2.50A in the Handbook of Procedures, 2023, prescribing the 
procedure for determining whether imported goods were produced using forced 
labour. 
These measures provide a legal and policy framework to prohibit the import of goods 
produced wholly or in part using forced labour and are designed to ensure that India's 
import policy remains consistent with the Constitution of India, relevant International 
Labour Organization (ILO) conventions, and international human rights standards, 
while safeguarding legitimate trade.

(a): Government is implementing various schemes to provide financial assistance and 
promote adoption of modern technologies such as precision farming and micro-irrigation. 
Details of some major schemes may be seen as under: 
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) is being implemented across the 
country for holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, vegetables, root and tuber 
crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic plants, coconut, cashew and cocoa. For adoption 
of modern technologies, financial assistance @ 50% of the eligible cost is provided under MIDH 
for construction of protected cultivation structures like poly house, shade net house, 
plastic/non-woven cloth tunnels, walk in tunnels, hydroponics and aeroponics etc.  Under 
MIDH, assistance is also provided for training on adoption of modern technologies through 
State Horticulture Missions, Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs), Centres of 
Excellence (CoEs), ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Krishi Vigyan 
Kendras (KVKs) and other recognized institutions. Centres of Excellence established under 
MIDH serve as demonstration and training centres and act as sources of elite planting material 
and vegetable seedlings under protected cultivation. Sixty-one (61) crop-specific Centres of 
Excellence have been established under MIDH through Indo-Israel Cooperation, Indo-Dutch 
Cooperation and Research Institutes.  

 
Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme promotes micro irrigation for enhancing water use 
efficiency at farm level and increasing productivity of crops and income of farmers through 
efficient water management. Financial assistance is provided to farmers @ 55% of the 
benchmark cost for Small and Marginal Farmers and 45% of the benchmark cost for other 
Farmers, for installation of micro-irrigation systems. The scheme also supports activities such 
as micro-irrigation demonstrations, capacity building, training, and awareness programmes to 
facilitate adoption of efficient irrigation technologies. Under the scheme, an area of 114.60 lakh 
hectares has been covered under micro irrigation since 2015-16.  
 
Government is implementing Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme across the 
country to mobilize a medium to long term debt financing facility for investment in viable 
projects relating to post harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets 
through incentives and financial support. Under AIF, there is provision for collateral free term 
loan upto Rs. 2.00 crore and interest subvention of 3% on the term loan availed for creation of 
post-harvest infrastructure, including establishment of hydroponics and aeroponics units.  
 
(b): Under Sub Mission for Agriculture Mechanization (SMAM), in order to make farm

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES

(a):  Under the the  Ministry of Textile's  National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), the 
scheme of "Grant for Research and Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical 
Textiles (GREAT)" aims to support the start -up ecosystem in the technical textiles sector by 
providing assistance to young innovators, scientists, technologists, and start -up ventures in 
translating their ideas into commercial technologies and products. The total budget allocated to 
the NTTM for the current financial year (2026-27) is Rs. 256 crore, which includes the provision 
for releasing grants to start-ups under the GREAT scheme.  

An Evaluation and Monitoring Committee (EMC) has been constituted under NTTM to evaluate, 
monitor, and review the technical and financial parameters of the start -up proposals. Based on 
the criteria laid out in the GREAT guidelines, the EMC submits its recommendations to the 
Empowered Programme Committee (EPC) under NTTM for approval of start -up proposals. 
GREAT guidelines are available at https://nttm.texmin.gov.in/.  
  
(b):  The grants provided to start -ups under NTTM are aimed at promoting innovation, 
commercialization of indigenous technologies, and the development of value -added technical 
textile products. The anticipated economic impact of these grants is fundamen tally driven by 
robust collaborations between the supported start -ups and established industry partners. By 
fostering strong synergies between innovators and industry stakeholders for prototype 
development, field trials, and market launches, the scheme ens ures market -ready 
commercialization. This active industry engagement is anticipated to successfully scale these 
start-ups, significantly strengthen the overall technical textiles ecosystem in the country, and 
thereby catalyze broader sustainable industry growth and employment generation. 
  
(c):  Under NTTM, a total of 31 start -ups have been approved at a total cost of Rs 15.40 
crore, of which Rs 13.65 crore is the Government of India share, details of which are given at 
Annexure-I. 
  
(d):  A Review and Monitoring Committee has been constituted to assess and oversee the 
progress of the approved start -ups, with the authority to recommend for release of subsequent 
instalments of grant and closure of projects to the Empowered Programme Committee under 
NTTM. Further, various public events, workshops, seminars and outreach activities are being 
organized nationwide to disseminate information about the scheme and facilitate industry 
engagement for scaling up the potential start-up projects.

GLOBAL CERTIFICATION FOR INDIAN SEAFOOD  
2611. Shri Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy: 
          Shri B K Pathasarathi: 
 
Will the MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the amount of funds sanctioned by the Government under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) 2.0 to support Indian fisheries in obtain ing global certifications 
such as the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certification; 
(b) the number of fisheries across India that have been provided such assistance, along with the 
total amount disbursed; 
(c) whether any fisheries from Andhra Pradesh hav e been assisted under this scheme for 
obtaining global certification, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the expected timeline for completion of certification and the estimated cost per fishery 
under this programme? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India  has been implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), a flagship scheme since FY 2020-21 for five years 
and the scheme has been extended up to September 2026 on the existing terms and conditions. 
The PMMSY supports obtaining certifications and traceability by funding the establishment of 
certification, accreditation, and comprehensive traceability systems using  IT applications and 
blockchain technology. Under PMMSY, financial assistance has been provided for 
certification, traceability, and accreditation of fish hatcheries, inland fish farms, and fish feed 
mills in six States, namely Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Gujarat, Assam, and 
Chhattisgarh, with a total outlay of ₹4.50 crore. Out of this, ₹1.68 crore has been approved for 
the Government of Andhra Pradesh. 
No proposal has been received from the Government of Andhra Pradesh seeking financial 
assistance under the PMMSY for obtaining global certifications such as Marine Stewardship 
Council (MSC)  certification. Further, no fisheries have been provided financial assistance 
under the PMMSY specifically for obtaining such global fishery certifications, and 
accordingly, no funds have been disbursed for this purpose.  

 
 
Ecolabelling and fishery certification schemes for marine capture fisheries are guided by the 
FAO Guidelines for the Ecolabelling of Fish and Fishery Products from Marine Capture 
Fisheries, whi ch outline internationally recognised principles and criteria for sustainable 
fisheries management. The Fishery Survey of India (FSI) and ICAR‑Central Marine Fisheries 
Research Institute (ICAR‑CMFRI) undertake periodic stock assessments and resource 
monitoring, providing the scientific basis required for sustainable fisheries management and 
credible certification initiatives. Under PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries is supporting 
strategic initiatives such as yellowfin tuna stock assessment by ICAR‑CMFRI an d marine 
mammal stock assessment and monitoring programmes by FSI. The Department has also 
endorsed the proposal of the Department of Fisheries, Lakshadweep, for obtaining MSC 
certification for the pole‑and‑line skipjack tuna fishery of Lakshadweep. In add ition to MSC, 
internationally recognised certification schemes such as Aquaculture Stewardship Council 
(ASC) and Best Aquaculture Practices (BAP)  are increasingly adopted in India, with several 
aquaculture farms, hatcheries, feed mills, and processing units already certified.

SDRF and NDRF is by way of relief and not for compensation. The details of 
the fund allocated and released under SDRF/NDRF to the States, are available 
on Disaster Management Division, Ministry of Home Aﬀairs' website i.e. 
ndmindia.mha.gov.in. 
 
In addition, the Government has introduced the yield -based Pradhan Mantri 
Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index based Restructured  Weather 
Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide 
financial support to farmers  suﬀering crop loss/damage arising out of natural 
calamities, adverse weather incidence and to stabilize the income of farmers 
etc. PMFBY provides for  comprehensive risk insurance against crop 
damage from pre sowing to post-harvest for crops and area notif ied by the 
concerned State Government. The scheme not only safeguards against wide 
spread yield loss due to non -preventable natural risks/ & extreme climate 
calamities viz. flood, inundation, landslide, drought, heat  waves, hailstorm, 
cyclone, pests/diseases, natural fire and lightening, storm,  typhoon, tempest, 
hurricane, tornado etc. but also, against farm level yield loss due to localized 
risks (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloud burst and natural fire) and post-
harvest losses due to cyclone, cyclonic/unseasonal rain and hailstorm and 
prevented sowing. 
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) implements a flagship network 
project National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) to 
strengthen climate resilience  in agriculture and to promote climate -resilient 
agricultural practices across the country. 
(c) & (d): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) through implementation 
of various initiatives and schemes  viz. Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA 
Yojana (PMKSY), Prime Minister Formalization of Micro Food Processing 
Enterprises (PMFME) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food 
Processing Industries (PLISFPI)

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO– 2615 
ANSWERED ON- 04.08.2026 
  
PANCHAYATI RAJ DEVOLUTION AND GRASSROOTS GOVERNANCE 
  
2615. ADV GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI: 
          DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH: 
SHRI VISHALDADA PRAKASHBAPU PATIL: 
MS. PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has undertaken an assessment, through the devolution Index, of the 
devolution of the 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule to Panchayati Raj Institutions, and 
if so, the details thereof, along with the reasons for the poor performing States in this regard, 
State/UT-wise;  
(b) whether the Ministry has taken any action to ensure that States/UTs effectively implement the 
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, and if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) the details and steps taken by the Ministry to curb the 'Sarpanch Pati' practice or proxy 
functioning in Panchayati Raj Institutions;  
(d) whether the Ministry has completed the collection of updated devolution index data from 
certain States which were unable to provide the same during the previous assessment and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
 (e) if so, the timeline of the release of the latest version of the Devolution Index? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH) 
  
(a) Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has released a report titled “Status of Devolution to 
Panchayats in States - An Indicative Evidence-Based Ranking, 2024” in February 2025 to assess 
the effectiveness of devolution and the role of local governments in strengthening grassroots 
democracy. This report presents the Devolution Index, which provides the overall scores and 
ranks for all States/Union Territories (UTs) covered under Part-IX of the Constitution, based on 
six identified dimensions: Framework, Functions, Finances, Functionaries, Capacity 
Enhancement, and Accountability. The dimension “Functions” includes the assessment of 
devolution of the 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. This 
report reveals that the extent of devolution has increased from 39.9% to 43.9% between the 

2 
 
period 2013-14 to 2021-22. Ranking of States/UTs in Devolution Index and Sub-indices is 
attached as Annexure-I. 
  
As per this report, States/UTs of Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Dadra & 
Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, Goa, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Ladakh, 
Lakshadweep, Manipur, Puducherry, and Punjab have been categorized as “Very Low (below 
National Average of 43.9)” on Devolution Index. The reason of their poor performance includes 
delay in elections, delays in delimitation, shortage of Staff, parastatal interference, inadequate 
training infrastructure and training activities and irregular constitution & delays in 
recommendations by State Finance Commissions etc.  
  
(b)  “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State List of Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operate through the respective 
State Panchayati Raj Acts. All the States/UTs, covered under Part-IX of the Constitution, have 
made their own Panchayati Raj Act, subject to the provisions of the Constitution. This Ministry 
has not received any reference/complaint from any State/UT for facing any difficulty in 
implementation of provisions of 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 incorporated as the 
Part IX of the Constitution. 
  
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has implemented a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely 
the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the 
objective of supporting Panchayati Raj institutions by imparting trainings to Elected 
Representatives and other stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby enabling Gram 
Panchayats to function effectively across all States/UTs. Under the scheme, capacity building 
support is provided to elected representatives, functionaries, and other stakeholders of 
Panchayats under different categories, viz. basic orientation and refresher programmes, thematic 
interventions, specialized trainings and Panchayat Development Plan-related programmes, etc. 
The scheme also supports exposure visits to facilitate experiential learning and replication of best 
practices for strengthening Panchayat governance, as well as development of training modules 
and materials etc. The Ministry also supplements the efforts of States/UTs on limited scale for 
creating basic infrastructure for effective functioning of Gram Panchayats such as Construction 
of Gram Panchayat Bhawans, Computers and Co-location of Common Service Centres (CSC) 
with Gram Panchayat Bhawans with focus on North East States, as proposed by States/UTs in 
their Annual Action Plans and later approved by Central Empowered Committee.

received, approved, funds sanctioned, released and utilised; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of natural farming on chemical fertiliser 
consumption under PM-PRANAM, if so, the State-wise details, classified district-wise for Uttar 
Pradesh including incentives released to Uttar Pradesh; 
(d) the number of Soil Health Cards issued in Uttar Pradesh during the last three years and the

(a) & (b):The progress made till date under National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) 
indicating the area, farmers and financial assistance released State-wise is given at Annexure – I. 
District-wise detail as reported by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh is given at Annexure - 
II. 

NMNF provides for setting up need-based Bio-input Resource Centres (BRCs).  The BRC 
may be setup nearby Goshalas for supply of the required quantities of urine and dung. BRCs 
provide ready-to-use Natural Farming bio-inputs for farmers who may not be making own on-farm 
inputs.  Bio-inputs enhance soil health and plant immunity and reduce dependence on chemical 
pesticides. Till date 83 BRCs has been setup in the State of Uttar Pradesh. 
(c): The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), on June 28, 2023, approved the 
“PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment, and Amelioration of 
Mother-Earth (PM-PRANAM)”. This initiative aims to preserve the health of Mother Earth 
through the promotion of sustainable and balanced fertilizer use, adoption of alternative 
fertilizers, promotion of organic farming and implementation of resource conservation 
technologies.  
Under PM-PRANAM Scheme, all States/UTs are covered including the State of Uttar 
Pradesh. There is a provision to provide incentives to States/UTs for reduction of consumption of 
chemical fertilizers (Urea, DAP, NPK, MOP) in a given financial year compared to the average 
consumption over the previous three years equivalent to 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved.  
Under PM-PRANAM scheme, 14 States/UTs (Karnataka, Maharashtra, West Bengal, 
Andhra Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, Tripura, 
Puducherry, Manipur, Goa, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Dadra and Nagar Haveli) have shown 
reduction of 15.14 Lakh Metric Tons of chemical fertilizer (Urea, DAP, NPKs & MoP) usage in 
2023-24 as compared to average consumption of previous 3 years. Similarly, 6 States/UTs 
(Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and 
Kashmir, Manipur) showed reduction in chemical fertilizer consumption by 0.49 LMT, in 2024-
25 as compared to the average consumption of previous 3 years. 5 States/UTs (Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli, Delhi, Goa, Manipur and Mizoram) showed a reduction of 0.18 Lakh Metric Tons 
chemical fertilizer usage in 2025-26 as compared to the average consumption of previous 3 years.  
(d): The number of Soil Health Cards (SHCs) issued in the State of Uttar Pradesh during the 
last three years is 4.85 Lakh in 2023-24, 8.26 Lakh in 2024-25, and 16.01 Lakh in 2025-26. 
Government promotes judicious use of fertilizer through Soil Health & Fertility scheme. The 
scheme provides Soil Health Cards (SHCs) for farm holdings to promote balanced and integrated 
nutrient management. In Uttar Pradesh 2,35,750 farmer’s trainings, 20,746 demonstrations, 
farmer’s 127 Melas/campaigns on soil health card recommendations have been organized to

Financial Health of Cooperative Societies 
2619. Shri Sanjay Dina Patil: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the functioning and financial health 
of cooperative societies operating in Mumbai during the last three years, including housing, 
consumer, credit and labour cooperatives;  
(b) the details of schemes implemented for digitisation, professional management, capacity 
building and governance reforms in cooperative institutions located in Mumbai;  
(c) whether the Government has identified challenges relating to transparency, elections, financial 
sustainability and member participation in cooperative societies functioning in Mumbai; and  
(d) the measures taken or proposed to strengthen cooperative governance, improve accountability, 
facilitate digital transformation and promote the cooperative movement in Mumbai? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD),  as on 15.07.2026,  there are  41,501 
cooperative societies in Mumbai, including housing, consumer, credit and labour cooperatives . 
Of these, 40,853 are functional. Among the functional cooperative societies, 19,911 are profit -
making and 14,877 are loss -making, while financial information is not available for 6,065 
societies. 
 
(b) The Government approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of functional 
Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) , including those in Maharashtra,  in 2022. The 
objective of the project is to bring all functional PACS on a common ERP (Enterprise Resource 
Planning)-based National Software. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the Project for 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Computerization of PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore. The project has since been 
expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore.  
Additionally, the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) provides financial 
assistance for infrastructure development, business diversification, value chain development, and 
capacity building of cooperative institutions across the country, inc luding Maharashtra. As on 
30.06.2026, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed ₹5,74,090.48 crore, including ₹3,96,763 crore 
during the last five years, for the development of cooperative institutions. 
 
(c) & (d) The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several 
initiatives to realize the vision of “Sahakar -se-Samriddhi” and to strengthen cooperative sector 
across the country including Mumbai. Key areas of initiatives include: 
 
(i). Computerization of PACS:  The Government has approved the Centrally Sponsored 
Project for Computerization of 79,630 PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore, 
along with provision of IT infrastructure and implementation guidelines (Margdarshika), 
to promote digitalization, transparency and efficient service delivery. 
(ii). Model Bye-laws for PACS: Enabled PACS to undertake more than 25 business activities, 
improve governance, transparency and accountability in their operations. Now, PACS can 
operate as PM-Kisan Samridhi Kendras (PMKSKs), Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi 
Kendras (PMBJKs), Common Service Centres (CSC) etc. 
(iii). Capacity Building and Training : Training programmes and workshops are organized 
for PACS officials to strengthen governance, financial management and operational 
capacity. 
(iv). Strengthening of the Three-Tier Cooperative Credit Structure: Measures have been 
taken to strengthen coordination among PACS, District Central Cooperative Banks 
(DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) to improve liquidity management and 
credit flow. 
(v). World's Largest Decentralized Grain Storage Plan: The Government is implementing 
the World's Largest Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector to enhance 
storage capacity at the grassroots level. 
(vi). National Cooperative Database (NCD): The NCD has been developed to identify gaps 
in cooperative coverage, facilitate formation of new cooperative societies, support 
evidence-based policymaking, and enable performance assessment of cooperative societies 
through the Cooperative Ranking Framework. 
(vii). Tribhuvan Sahkari University : The Government has established Tribhuvan Sahkari 
University to strengthen cooperative education, training, research and capacity building.

fibres, yarns and raw materials through fabric and apparel manufacturing to finished, export -
ready products, enabling buyers to engage with the complete textile value chain under a single

(b): The Bharat Tex serves as a platform for facilitating Business -to-Business (B2 B),

for manufacturers, exporters, artisan groups, handloom and handicraft clu sters, MSMEs, global

together weavers and artisans from across the country, providing them with a dedicated platform 
to interact with domestic and international buyers and expand their market outreach.

invited to participate in the event, providing them exposure to the broader textile ecosystem, 
emerging market trends, technological innovations and ne tworking opportunities with industry 
leaders, buyers and institutional stakeholders. Together, these initiatives sought to foster 
inclusive participation and create greater market access for stakeholders across different 
segments of the textile sector.

Bharat Tex 2026. The pavilion showcased the State's rich textile and handicraft traditions, 
handloom products, regional clusters, industrial capabilities and investm ent opportunities before 
domestic and international buyers, global brands, industry leaders and investors. It also 
highlighted the State's efforts to promote traditional crafts alongside modern textile value chains. 
(d):  Bharat Tex 2026 featured a dedicat ed Eco -Stitch Sustainability & Circularity Hub, 
presented jointly by the Clothing Manufacturers Association of India (CMAI) and the Global 
Alliance for Textile Sustainability (GATS), under the theme “Sustainable, Circular and 
Competitive Bharat.” The Hub c omprised six curated zone, the India Impact Wall, Circularity at 
Scale, From Waste to Global Wardrobe, Made in Circular Bharat, the Material & Innovation 
Library, and the Circular Bharat Forum, bringing together recyclers, manufacturers, brands,

DISTRICTS INCLUDED UNDER NATIONAL HORTICULTURE MISSION 
2625.  SMT. MANJU SHARMA: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of districts included under the Horticulture Mission in Rajasthan; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to extend the said Mission to the remaining 
districts also, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c)  whether the Government has received any representations from many other States 
to include more districts under the said mission; and 
(d)  if so, the steps taken by the Government in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी           (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): National Horticulture Mission (NHM) under the Mission for Integrated Development 
of Horticulture (MIDH) is being implemented by Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 
since 2014 for the holistic development of horticulture in the country. Pursuant to the 
revision of the Operational Guidelines of MIDH in 2025, all districts of Rajasthan are 
covered under the Mission. 
 
(b) to (d): Prior to the revision of the Operational Guidelines of MIDH in 2025, National 
Horticulture Mission (NHM) was implemented in selected districts identified on the basis of 
comparative advantage of horticulture crops, agro-climatic suitability and potential for 
development of marketing linkages. Since the launch of MIDH in 2014-15, the Government 
received representations from various States seeking inclusion of additional districts under 
the Mission. Taking into account the implementation experience of the Mission and the 
representations received from the States, the Operational Guidelines of MIDH were revised 
in 2025, extending the coverage of the Mission to all districts in all States and Union 
Territories. Accordingly, all districts are now eligible for assistance under the Mission in 
accordance with the Operational Guidelines.

ILLEGAL FISHERIES 
2628. SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study/surveys to identify and assess illegal 
fisheries in the country; 
(b) if so, the details regarding the number of illegal fisheries detected during the last five years, 
State-wise and district-wise in Andhra Pradesh and in Eluru District in Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) the details regarding the enforcement action taken against illegal fisheries during the last five 
years, including the number of units shut down across the country, State-wise and district wise 
in Andhra Pradesh and in Eluru District; and 
(d) the details regarding the measures undertaken by the Government to prevent and reduce 
illegal fisheries and undertake awareness programmes for fishers and coastal communities? 
 
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) to (c): ‘Fisheries’ is a state subject, and each Coastal State has enacted its Marine Fishing 
Regulation Act (MFRA) for governance of fishing activities within the territorial waters up to 
12 nautical miles from the baseline. The regulation of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone 
(EEZ) beyond territorial waters is governed by the Union Government through the Maritime 
Zones of India (Regulation of fishing by foreign vessels) Act, 1981 and the  Sustainable 
Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone of India Rules, 2025. Government of 
Andhra Pradesh has informed that the Andhra Pradesh Marine Fishing Regulation  Act (AP-
MFRA) and AP-MFR Rules are implemented to curb the illegal fishing in the territorial waters 
of Andhra Pradesh and the details of district wise violations of the AP-MFRA across the state 
during the last 4 years are Annexed. It is further informed that Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh 
has no coastline.  
The Government of Andhra Pradesh has  also informed that there is a continuous intrusion of 
mechanized fishing boats from Tamil Nadu and Puducherry in the territorial waters of Andhra 
Pradesh near south coastal districts i.e., Tirupathi, SPSR Nellore, Prakasam and Bapatla and 
around 160 cases of i llegal fishing have been reported during last 5 years.  Government of 
Andhra Pradesh has informed that in 2022-23, a penalty amounting to Rs. 52,500 was collected 
and fish catch worth Rs.31000 was confiscated from 21 fishing boats from Srikakulam, Krishna, 
Bapatla and Prakasam Districts, in 2024-25, a penalty of Rs. 7500 was collected and fish catch 
worth Rs.5000 was confiscated from 3 fishing boats from Bapatla District and in 2025-26, Rs. 
2500 was collected and fish catch worth Rs.2500 was confiscated from  1 Fishing boat from  
Kakinada District for violation of fishing ban period.  

 
(d): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) has issued advisories from 
time to time to all the coastal States/UTs for preventing juvenile fishing and ban on destructive 
fishing practices for ensuring sustainability. Paired bottom trawling or bull trawling and use of 
LED lights in fishing are banned in the EEZ of India. All the maritime States/UTs have also 
been advised to take necessary steps to prevent pair o r bull trawling and use of LED light for 
fishing within and beyond the territorial waters. Besides, the DoF, GoI has also advised to 
coastal states/UTs to review and amend their respective MFRAs to ensure mandatory use of 
Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) tow ards marine turtle conservation. The implementation of 
TED has been included and supported under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) with 100% financial assistance (60% Central and 40% State).  The Sustainable 
Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone Rules , 2025 are framed to promote 
sustainability of marine ecosystem with optimum utilization of untapped fishery resources. 
Emphasis is also given to promote ecosystem approach for sustainable harnessing of resources 
in the EEZ, and implementation of the conservation and management measures, such as uniform 
ban on fishing during monsoon or fish breeding season, minimum legal size of fish, bycatch 
reduction, best practices for reducing post -harvest losses, conservation of fish stocks or 
rejuvenation measures including sea ranching, installation of artificial reefs, etc. The Rules also 
prohibit destructive fishing and juvenile fishing in the EEZ to protect the marine biodiversity 
of our seas.  
The DoF, GoI issues advisory to coastal States and Union Territories (UTs) from time to time 
to sensitize the fishermen for prevention of crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line

REDUCING CARBON EMISSIONS 
 
2629. DR. PRABHA MALLIKARJUN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has prepared any roadmap for reducing carbon emissions from energy -
intensive manufacturing and heavy industries sectors;  
 
(b) the details of schemes and programmes promoting adoption of green technologies, industrial 
energy efficiency and renewable energy integration during the last five years;  
 
(c) the details of amount of financial assistance, incentives and budgetary support provided for 
industrial decarbonisation projects, State-wise;  
 
(d) the details of expected contribution of such initiatives towards achieving India's climate 
commitments and industrial sustainability goals; and  
 
(e) whether industries located in Karnataka, including industrial units operating in and around 
Davanagere district, have benefited from such programmes and the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (e): Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change has informed that India’s 
Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement aims for a reduction in the 
emission intensity of its GDP and is not sector -specific. Accordingly, no sector-specific roadmap for 
reducing greenhouse gas emissions from energy -intensive manufacturing and heavy industries is 
prescribed under the NDC framework document.  
 
The Government promotes low -carbon development through the convergence of various 
schemes and programmes relating to energy efficiency, renewable energy, green hydrogen, and 
resource efficiency. The National Action Plan on Cl imate Change (NAPCC) and State Action Plans 
on Climate Change (SAPCC) provide the overarching framework for these actions. Eligible industries 
across states, including Karnataka, can avail of benefits under applicable schemes subject to respective 
guidelines.  
 
As a result of cumulative national measures, India successfully decoupled its economic growth 
from greenhouse gas emissions. As per India's First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR), the emission 
intensity of GDP declined by 37.38% in 2022 from the 20 05 level. Furthermore, India's non -fossil 
fuel-based cumulative installed electric power capacity has crossed 50%, achieving this milestone five 
years ahead of the 2030 target.  
 
Further, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), a CPSE under Ministry of He avy 
Industries  continuously implements measures to reduce its carbon footprint. These include Improving 
energy efficiency across its manufacturing facilities; i ncreasing renewable energy adoption; 
generating nearly 276 million units of electricity from in-house solar installations over the last 9 years; 
creating carbon sinks by planting over 44,000 saplings in FY 2025 -26 alone; r educing waste and 
developing efficient, low-emission technologies for the power, industry, and transportation sectors.

OILSEED AND PALM OIL PRODUCTION 
 
2630. COM. SELVARAJ V:  
SHRI SUBBARAYAN K: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether it is a fact that a national mission is launched in November 2024 aiming to 
boost primary oil seeds production from 39 MT in 2022-23 to 69.7 MT by 2030-31; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and to what extent this target has been achieved so far; 
(c)  whether it is a fact that the palm oil shipments accounts for about 47% of the total 
imports of about 16 MT cooking oil in 2024-25 oil year; and 
(d)  the details of measures being taken to raise the palm oil production in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b):  The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was approved on 
3rd October, 2024 to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive towards self-reliance 
(Atmanirbhar Bharat) in edible oils. The mission aims to increase primary oilseed 
production from 39 million tonnes (2022-23) to 69.7 million tonnes by 2030-31. 
 
The NMEO-OS is implemented through a cluster-based approach. Over 600 Value Chain 
Cluster have been identified across the country which is managed by Value Chain Partners 
such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under 
these clusters, farmers are provided free high-quality seeds of latest high yielding varieties 
and training on good agricultural practices. The mission supports the establishment and 
upgradation of post-harvest infrastructure (oil mills) to improve oil recovery from primary 
and secondary sources. 
 
The mission strengthens availability of certified seeds through 100% support for purchase 
of breeder seeds, establishment of new seed hubs and specialised seed storage units in 
the public sector to enhance production and storage capacity. 

 
The mission focuses on improving productivity through Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs), 
Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLDs) and Block-Level Demonstrations (BLDs) to help 
farmers adopt latest varieties and good agricultural practices. 
 
Oilseed production has increased from 39.67 million tonnes in 2023-24 to 43.06 million 
tonnes in 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW). Under the mission, 13.52 lakh hectares 
were covered under free seed distribution in Value Chain Clusters during 2025-26, against 
the annual target of 10.00 lakh hectares. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units 
have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seed of recently released varieties.  
 
(c) & (d):  As reported by the Directorate of Sugar & Vegetable Oils, Department of Food 
and Public Distribution, India imported 160.72 lakh tonnes of edible oils during 2024–25. Of 
this, 75.17 lakh tonnes comprised palm oil, accounting for 46.77% of the total edible oil 
imports.  
 
The Government of India launched the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-
OP) in August 2021 to promote oil palm cultivation, with special focus on North Eastern 
States. The Mission is being implemented in 15 States. The mission provides 
comprehensive support to farmers, including assistance for high quality planting materials, 
inputs for intercropping and maintenance during the four year gestation period. There is 
also a provision for replanting of old and unproductive plantations. The mission supports 
farm machinery, irrigation facilities, seed gardens, nurseries and Custom Hiring Centres. 
The North Eastern States are provided financial assistance for setting up oil palm 
processing mills.  
 
From 2021-22 to 2025-26, 2.73 lakh hectares was brought under oil palm cultivation, taking 
the cumulative area to 6.40 lakh hectares as on 31.03.2026. During this period, 114.66 lakh 
tonnes of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) were harvested, resulting in the production of 20.10 
lakh tonnes of Crude Palm Oil (CPO). At present, 27 oil palm processing mills are 
operational across the country. The Mission provides Viability Gap Payment (VGP) to 
support oil palm growers. As on date, ₹18.90 crore has been disbursed to 9,244 oil palm 
farmers in Goa, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and 
Mizoram under this provision.

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is implementing Mission 
for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) throughout the country including 
in the State of Andhra Pradesh, under which financial assistance is provided for 
establishment of various horticulture activities such as Establishment of New 
Gardens, Creation of Water Resources, Protected Cultivation, Integrated Post-
Harvest Management, Centre of Excellence (CoE), Marketing, Beekeeping, and 
Horticulture Mechanization. 
 
 Further, Government is implementing various interventions through Coconut 
Development Board for the integrated development of coconut sector in the country 
wherein financial assistance is provided @ Rs. 56000 per hectare for new coconut 
plantation.  

 
In addition, National Mission on Edible-Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) is being 
implemented in 15 States including Rajahmundry region of Andhra Pradesh to 
promote oil palm cultivation and achieve Aatmanirbhar Bharat in edible oils. The 
Mission provides comprehensive support to farmers, including assistance for high-
quality planting material, inputs for intercropping, and maintenance during the four-
year gestation period, as well as replanting of old and unproductive plantations.  
Additional inputs such as farm machinery and irrigation facilities are also supported.  
Furthermore, the scheme promotes the establishment of seed gardens, nurseries, 
and custom hiring centres, while North-Eastern States receive additional support for 
setting up oil palm processing mills.  
 
     During 2025-26, an amount of Rs. 179.82 Lakhs was utilized in Andhra Pradesh 
under CDB scheme, out of which Rs. 2.94 Lakhs was utilized in Rajahmundry region 
covering 10.50 ha of coconut plantation. Under Oil Palm scheme, an amount of Rs. 
9.42 crore has been distributed for expanding oil palm cultivation in Rajahmundry 
region. Under MIDH, an amount of Rs. 13.31 Lakhs has been utilized for area 
expansion of citrus and dragon fruit in Rajahmundry region.  
 
(c): Under the Post Harvest Management (PHM) component of MIDH scheme, 
during 2025-26, two (02) Pack houses have been established in East Godavari 
District.  
 
    Further, Government is implementing Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) 
scheme across the country to mobilize a medium to long term debt financing facility 
for investment in viable projects relating to post harvest management infrastructure 
and community farming assets through incentives and financial support. Under AIF, 
there is provision for collateral free term loan upto Rs. 2.00 crore and interest 
subvention of 3% on the term loan availed for creation of post-harvest infrastructure, 
including establishment of cold storages. Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund

Sorting & Grading Units, 10 Assaying Units, 7 Silos, 7 Post-Harvest Management

Packaging Unit.

2632.  SHRI SANATAN PANDEY: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the level of competition in sectors 
where a few large business groups have significant market presence; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether any measures have been taken to facilitate the participation of MSMEs 
and new entrants in Government tenders; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof along with the outcome of such measures? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b): The Competition Commission of India (CCI) under the Ministry of Corporate 
Aﬀairs conducts market studies from time to time to develop  a better 
understanding of competitive conditions within one or more sectors. These 
studies enable CCI to gauge market developments, track evolving competition 
dynamics, understand specific business practices and analyse implications for 
competition arising from structural features.  In the past, CCI has carried out 
market studies in various sectors/areas including e -Commerce, Telecom, Cab 
Aggregation and Artificial Intelligence. 
(c) & (d): The Government has taken following measures to facilitate the participation 
of MSMEs and new entrants in Government tenders: - 
 As per the  Public Procurement Policy Order, 2012, the target for 
procurement from Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) is 25%. As 
reported by  Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) on SAMBANDH 
portal, procurement by CPSEs from MSEs has been 49.05% in 2025-26. 
 GeM has implemented the following measures to facilitate the participation 
of MSMEs on GeM portal; 
 
i. GeM has integration with Udyam database to verify and update 
status of sellers as MSMEs. 
ii. In case of direct purchase from Marketplace, buyers are provided with 
the marketplace filters to identify the products offered by MSMEs. 
iii. In line with Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises 
(MSEs) order, 2012 functionality provided for reserving the bid for 
procurement from MSEs, giving purchase preference and relaxation in 
Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)/ prior experience/ turnover.

2633.  SHRI JASWANTSINH SUMANBHAI BHABHOR: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  the details of achievements and success of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi 
(PM-KISAN) scheme in economically empowering the farmers of Dahod Lok Sabha 
Constituency;  
(b)  the total number of farmers who have directly benefited from this visionary scheme in 
the said region since its inception, year-wise;  
(c)  the total amount of funds successfully transferred directly into the bank accounts of 
farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), ensuring transparent distribution in the 
Dahod parliamentary constituency;  
(d)  the details of the proactive steps taken and special saturation drives conducted by 
the Government to ensure 100% registration of eligible tribal and marginal farmers in the 
Dahod Lok Sabha Constituency; and  
(e)  the overall positive socio-economic impact of this continuous financial assistance 
with regard to agricultural productivity, procurement of agricultural inputs, and the livelihood 
of the farming community in the region? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e):      The PM-KISAN scheme is a central sector scheme launched to supplement 
the financial needs of farmers with cultivable land-holding. Under the scheme, a financial 
benefit of ₹ 6,000/- per year is transferred in three equal instalments, into the Aadhaar 

seeded bank accounts of farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. Under the 
PM-KISAN Scheme, Government of India has disbursed over ₹ 4.47 lakh Cr. to the 
beneficiaries through 23 installments since inception of the Scheme.  
As per the impact evaluation study by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation 
Office (DMEO) of NITI Aayog, the scheme is successfully fulfilling its primary function of 
providing direct financial assistance to farmers holding agricultural land, thereby enhancing 
their economic stability and agricultural productivity. The study also shows that over 92 
percent of beneficiary farmers utilized the financial assistance for essential agricultural 
inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides, which are particularly important in the face 
of rising input costs and weather-related uncertainties. 
  
Instalment-wise details of beneficiaries benefitted in Dahod and Mahisagar districts 
of Gujarat and amount released to them since inception is at Annexure. 
 
 In order to ensure that no eligible farmer,  including tribal and marginal farmers, is 
left out, the Government of India undertakes saturation drives in coordination with the 
States/UTs, including Gujarat. A major nationwide saturation drive was undertaken from 
15th November 2023 under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra (VBSY), during which, more 
than 1 Cr. farmers were included under PM-KISAN. Further, under the Government’s 100 
days initiative in 2024, over 25 lakh eligible farmers were added under the PM-KISAN 
scheme. A special drive was also conducted in September 2024 to clear the pending self-
registration cases, which resulted in the addition of over 30 lakh new farmers. Further, a 
nationwide saturation drive was undertaken in June, 2026 under PM-KISAN, alongwith the 
“Khet Bachao Abhiyaan” to expand the coverage of eligible farmers under the scheme, 
which resulted in the addition of about 17 lakh farmers in the country, including 1 lakh 
farmers in Gujarat, including Dahod.

GLOBALLY IMPORTANT AGRICULTURAL HERITAGE SYSTEMS 
2635. SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the financial, technical and institutional assistance provided by the 
Government to the Kuttanad Agricultural Heritage System, Kerala, after its recognition as a 
Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) site by the Food and Agriculture 
Organization (FAO); 
(b) the details of the projects sanctioned, funds allocated and expenditure incurred for the 
conservation and sustainable development of the Kuttanad GIAHS site, year-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has formulated or proposes to formulate a dedicated action 
plan for the conservation, climate resilience, branding and promotion of the Kuttanad 
Agricultural Heritage System and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether consultations have been held with the Government of Kerala and other 
stakeholders for the long-term conservation and management of the site; and 
(e) the further steps proposed to strengthen and promote Kuttanad as a globally significant 
agricultural heritage landscape? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a) &  (b): As reported by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), India, the Kuttanad 
Farming System in Kerala was recognized as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage 
System (GIAHS) in 2013 under the FAO’s GIAHS Programme. 
As reported by the Government of Kerala, Kuttanad has been declared as a Special 
Agricultural Zone by the State Government. A comprehensive Kuttanad Package for 
mitigation of agrarian distress and restoration of the Kuttanad wetland ecosystem was 
implemented during 2008–2019 through more than 14 implementing agencies. Funding was 
mobilised through various Central Ministries and schemes, Government of Kerala Plan 
schemes and Finance Commission grants. As reported by the Kerala State Planning Board, 
expenditure of about ₹1,013.35 crore had been incurred under the Package up to 31 March 
2019. 
The International Research and Training Centre for Below Sea Level Farming 
(IRTCBSF) at Alappuzha undertakes research relating to climate change and salinity 
intrusion in Kuttanad and develops technologies for improving productivity and farmers’ 
income. Under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (Detailed Project Report 
Component), a project titled “Ecological Utilization of Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) 
in Kuttanad” was sanctioned during 2022-23 with a project cost of ₹1,513 lakh, against which 
₹107.52 lakh has been released. 

 
The Government of India also supports sustainable agriculture, conservation of agro-
biodiversity, climate resilience and farmers’ livelihoods through various Central Sector and 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Farmers and institutions in the Kuttanad region are eligible 
for assistance under these schemes, subject to the respective scheme guidelines and the 
priority proposed by the State Government in the Annual Action Plan of the State. Details of 
relevant projects and assistance reported in respect of the Kuttanad region are given in the 
Annexure. 
In addition, the Ministry of Jal Shakti implemented two flood mitigation projects for 
Padasekharams of the Kuttanad region during 2014-15 and 2017-18 at a total cost of ₹54.63 
crore. 
The Government of Kerala has further reported implementation of the following State 
Plan schemes in the Kuttanad region: 
(i) Development of Agriculture Sector in Kuttanad, with a budget provision of ₹7 crore during 
2025-26 for strengthening paddy field infrastructure. Since 2020-21, an expenditure of 
₹2,017.55 lakh has been incurred for replacement of traditional Petti and Para systems with 
Vertical Axial Flow (VAF) pump sets. 
(ii) Rebuild Kerala Initiative Project for sustainable development of the Kuttanad rice 
ecosystem and integrated farming, with an outlay of ₹203 lakh. 
(iii) Assistance to Paddy Cultivation in Kuttanad, under which financial assistance is 
provided to paddy farmers. 
(iv) Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (NABARD) General, under which two 
infrastructure projects with a total outlay of ₹1,800 lakh are under implementation. 
(c) to (e): The Government of India continues to support the Kuttanad region through various 
ongoing Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes, under which assistance is 
available for sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, farm mechanization, water 
management, infrastructure development and farmers’ livelihoods, subject to the provisions 
of the respective schemes and the priority proposed by the State Government in the Annual 
Action Plan of the State.

(a) to (c) Under the scheme ‘Integrated Coffee Development Project (ICDP)’ Coffee 
Board undertakes various activities for promotion of coffee  that inter alia include 
participation in international trade fairs/events; capacity building programs; 
entrepreneurship development programs; organization of coffee tasting sessions and 
training programs on barista skills; generic branding of Indian coffee for premiumization; 
digital media / social media campaigns for branding and promotion; support for value -
addition; organizing Buyer-Seller meets in association with Indian Missions abroad and 
promotion of value added coffees sold in retail packs (upto 10 00 Gms) which have 
‘Coffees of India’ logo and also depict the words indicating ‘Made in India’ on the retail 
packs.   Further, the Coffee Board also promotes GI coffees and has developed 
Gourmet GI Coffee Gift Boxes in collaboration with Indian Missions abroad to enhance 
the domestic and international visibility of Indian GI coffees. In order to promote Indian 
coffees in different regions of the world Coffee Board has participated in 41 international 
fairs from 2018 -19 onwards that inter alia include event s such as Gulf food, Dubai, 
World of Coffee, Amsterdam, Melbourne International Coffee Expo, Host Milano, World 
Specialty Coffee Conference & Exhibition Tokyo, International Café Show Seoul etc. 

2 
 
Indian coffee was exported to more than 140 countries during FY 2025 –26 with a 
significant increase in coffee exports to emerging and expanding markets such as 
United Arab Emirates, Libya, Australia, South Korea, Egypt, Kuwait and United 
Kingdom and new markets such as Djibouti, Micronesia, Timor-Leste etc. 
  
(d) to  (f) Government undertakes several initiatives to enhance the visibility and 
marketability of GI products that inter alia include organization of India GI fair, GI 
Mahotsav & GI Pavilions at national & international exhibitions. Further, Coffee Board 
has u ndertaken several initiatives to promote GI -tagged coffees and support coffee 
growers for cultivating GI -registered coffees, including those in Wayanad Lok Sabha 
Constituency. The 'Wayanad Robusta Coffee' is registered as Geographical Indication. 
The Coffee Board is the Authorized User Registrar for GI-tagged coffees and conducts 
regular awareness programmes on GI user registration for all stakeholders across the 
coffee value chain. It also organizes GI coffee tasting sessions, Buyer-Seller Meets and 
participates in coffee -centric trade fairs and food & beverage events to promote GI -
tagged coffees. The initiatives also interalia include development support to growers, 
including small and tribal coffee farmers under Coffee Board’s ICDP scheme.  During 
FY 2025 –26, the average export unit values of GI -registered Arabica and Robusta 
coffees increased by 34.36% and 29.73%, respectively, compared to FY 2024–25. The 
details of Indian Coffee varieties that have received Geographical Indications (GI), 
state-wise, are attached as Annexure-I.

(a) & (b) Krishonnati Yojana (KY) is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare comprising several flagship interventions, 
including the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM), Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE), National 
Mission on Edible Oil-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS), National Mission on Edible Oil-Oilpalm (NMEO-
OP), Sub-Mission on Seeds & Planting Material (SMSP), Digital Agriculture Mission, Mission 
for Atmanirbharta in Pulses, Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern 
Region (MOVCDNER) and  Integrated Scheme on Agricultural Marketing (ISAM). 
The overarching objective of Krishonnati Yojana is to promote holistic, sustainable and 
inclusive development of the agriculture sector by enhancing agricultural production and 
productivity, promoting quality seeds and planting materials, supporting crop diversification, 
horticulture and agroforestry, strengthening agricultural marketing and post-harvest 
infrastructure, facilitating digital agriculture and data-driven governance,  extension services 
and markets, ensuring food and nutritional security. The details of implementation of  
Krishonnati Yojana is placed at Annexure I. 
 
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Mission on Natural Farming is being 
implemented since November, 2024 to promote natural farming across the country. Natural 
Farming (NF) is a chemical free farming, involving livestock (preferably local breed of cow) 
integrated natural farming methods and diversified crop systems rooted in the Indian traditional 
knowledge. It is aimed towards improving soil health and restoring ecosystems and reducing 
input cost to the farmer to achieve greater climate resilience. The objectives of the Mission 
are: - 

 
i. To promote nature based sustainable systems of farming, enhancing usage of on-farm 
made natural farming bio-inputs, to reduce dependency on externally purchased inputs 
and input cost reduction, to also improve soil health and have sustainable agriculture 
practices. 
ii. To popularize livestock (preferably local breed of cow) integrated agriculture-animal 
husbandry models. 
iii. To strengthen on-farm agroecological research and knowledge based extension 
capacities of ICAR institutions, KVKs, Agricultural Universities, etc. 
iv. To build upon the on-field experience of practicing Natural Farming farmers and scientific 
expertise to thereby evolve & improvise location specific NF package of practices for 
increased spread of NF. 
v. To establish scientifically supported common standards and easy farmer friendly 
certification procedures for naturally grown chemical-free produce. 
vi. To create and promote a single national brand for naturally grown chemical-free 
produce. 
The details of implementation of National Mission on Natural Farming is placed at Annexure 
II. 
The Government is implementing National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM) for 
promotion of scientific beekeeping and holistic development of beekeeping sector across the 
country.  The Mission aims to increase honey production and productivity, improve the quality 
and traceability of honey and other bee products, strengthen production and processing 
infrastructure, promote research, capacity building and entrepreneurship, create employment 
opportunities and augment farmers’ income by promoting beekeeping as a viable allied 
agricultural activity. NBHM is a demand-driven, project-based Central Sector Scheme under 
which financial assistance is provided to eligible implementing agencies as per the scheme 
guidelines. No State-wise allocation of funds is made under the Mission. The details of 
implementation of National Beekeeping and Honey Mission is placed at Annexure III. 
 
(c) & (d) Presently, the Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of Agriculture & 
Farmers’ Welfare are implemented under two umbrella schemes, namely Pradhan Mantri-
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) and Krishonnati Yojana (KY).

(b): The actuarial/bidded/tendered  premium rates are charged by implementing agencies

maximum 5% of sum insured for commercial/horticultural crops.  Remaining part of

assistance to make the scheme affordable to farmers.    

From Kharif 2023, 3 Alternate Risk Transfer Models (ARTM) other than standard 
PMFBY namely, cup and cap model (80:110), cup and cap model (60:130) and profit and 
loss sharing model have been implemented under which in case of claims below certain 
threshold, portion of the premium paid by the Government as subsidy will go back to the 
Government and in case of claims above the threshold, Government are required to pay 
the additional claims.  Total liability of State and Central Government is dependent on the 
total claims generated in different clusters of a State and the ARTM model adopted by the 
State based on which excess premium becomes recoverable or claim liability becomes 
due. 
Total premium collected by insurance companies from farmers, States and Central 
Government during last five years i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26 under the scheme is

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4TH AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 13, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
PROVISIONS IN BNS TO DEAL CRIMES  
 
2645 # SHRI DILIP SAIKIA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any provisions have been made under the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita (B.N.S.) 2023 to deal with crimes against women and children in 
stringent manner; and  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government is committed to prevention and countering of the 
crime against women and children. In the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, 
for the first time, the provisions relat ing to crime against woman and child 
have been given precedence and placed under one Chapter. Strict 
punishments up to death sentence have been provided for the offences 
against women. Punishment for gang rape of a woman below the age of 18 
years is life imprisonment till remainder of the convict’s natural life or death. 
A new offence for having sexual intercourse on false promise of marriage, 
employment, promotion or by concealing identity, etc. has also been 
incorporated in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Main provisions related to 
protection of women and children in the new sanhitas are given in Annexure. 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2645 FOR 04.08.2026 
Annexure 
 
PROVISIONS FOR PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN   
 
i. Offences against woman and child have been given  precedence over 
all other offences in a new chapter-V of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. 
 
ii. In Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the age differential for minor victims of 
gang rape has been done away with. Earlier different punishments 
were prescribed for gang rape on a girl below the age of 16 years and 
12 years. This provision has been modified and now gang rape on a 
woman below the age of eighteen years is punishable with 
imprisonment of life or death. 
 
iii. Women have been recognized as an adult member of family who can 
receive summons on behalf of the person summoned. The earlier 
reference to ‘some adult male member’ has been replaced with ‘some 
adult member’. 
 
iv. In order to provide more protection to the victim and enforce 
transparency in investigation r elated to an offence of rape, the 
statement of the victim shall be recorded through audio video means 
by police. 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2645 FOR 04.08.2026 
 
v. For certain offences against woman, statement of the victim is to be 
recorded, as far as practicable, by  a woman Magistrate and in her 
absence a male Magistrate in the presence of a woman to ensure 
sensitivity and fairness, creating a supportive environment for victims. 
 
vi. Medical practitioners are mandated  to send the medical report of a 
victim of rape to the investigating officer within 7 days. 
 
vii. It is provided that no male person under the age of fifteen years or 
above the age of 60 years (65 years earlier) or a woman or a mentally 
or physically disabled p erson or a person with acute illness shall be 
required to attend at any place other than the place in which such male 
person or woman resides. In cases where such a person is willing to 
attend the police station, they may be allowed to do so. 
 
viii. The new laws provide for free first-aid or medical treatment to victims 
of crimes against women and children at all hospitals. This provision 
ensures immediate access to essential medical care, prioritizing the 
well-being and recovery of victims during challenging times. 
 
 

 
-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2645 FOR 04.08.2026 
 
ix. The act of hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence, 
is made a punishable offence under section 95 of Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita 2023, which entails punishment of imprisonment of minimum 
seven years, extendable to ten years. This provision aims to deter 
gangs or groups from employing/hiring children for committing offence.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2648 
ANSWERED ON 04.08.2026 
 
HIGH-SPEED EV CHARGING INFRASTRUCTURE ON NATIONAL HIGHWAYS 
 
2648. DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has finalized the locations for the 2,000 high -speed charging stations 
sanctioned for major national highways by February 2026, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether the Government is providing a 100% capital grant for the installation of these chargers 
in public-private partnership (PPP) mode, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether these charging stations are being equipped with "Open Charging Point Protocol" (OCPP) 
to ensure compatibility across all EV brands;  
 
(d) whether the Government is collaborating with the Govt of Power to ensure dedicated green-energy 
feeders for these high-speed charging hubs, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(e) whether this infrastructure rollout led to a measurable increase in the sales of long -range electric 
heavy vehicles and passenger cars, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): There is an allocation of Rs.2,000 crore under the PM E-DRIVE scheme for deployment of adequate 
number of EV public charging stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including major national highways. There 
is no target number of charging stations for national highways.  
 
(b): Under the PM E -DRIVE Scheme, 100% capital grant is provided only for “Category A" 
locations, comprising Central Government and State Government premises, including government 
offices, government residential complexes, and Central Public Se ctor Enterprises (CPSEs), subject 
to unrestricted public access for EV charging. 
 
(c): To ensure broad compatibility across all electric vehicle brands, EV charging stations funded 
by the PM E-DRIVE scheme are equipped with the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP). 
 
(d): No such proposal is under consideration.  
 
(e): Yes. EV sales have shown a consistent upward trend during the period 2019 –20 to 2025–26, 
and overall EV penetration has increased from 0.68% in 2019–20 to 8.26% in FY 2025–26.  However, 
no assessment has been carried out by MHI to establish a direct causal relationship between the rollout 
of the charging infrastructure and the increase in sales of EVs.
