CHALLENGES IN TRADITIONAL FARMING 
 
2657.  SHRI EATALA RAJENDER: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Bio-technology addresses challenges in traditional farming by enhancing 
crop resilience, improving yields and fostering sustainability through tools like genetically 
modified (GM) crops, bio-fertilizers and molecular breeding and these innovations help 
combat climate change, reduce reliance on synthetic pesticides and improve nutrient 
absorption; 
(b)  if so, the details of the steps taken and results yielded in this regard; 
(c)  whether the Bio-technology offers green growth prospects in agriculture industry and 
if so, the details thereof and views of experts in this regard; and 
(d)  whether it is also a fact that given the population growth and climate change, there 
are challenges to traditional farming practices and food security, which can be addressed 
with the application of biotechnology; and 
(e)  if so, the details of the steps taken and foreign assistance received, funds sanctioned 
and utilised therefor?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): As reported by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), several 
research, development and capacity-building initiatives have been undertaken to harness 
biotechnology for enhancing agricultural productivity, resilience and sustainability. These 
initiatives include research on molecular breeding, genomics, marker-assisted selection, 
genome editing, molecular diagnostics and genetic resource characterization through ICAR 

Institutes, All India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRPs), All India Network Projects 
(AINPs) and Consortia Research Platform Projects (CRPs). The major outcomes of these 
initiatives include development and dissemination of bio-fertilizers such as Rhizobium, 
Azotobacter, Azospirillum, phosphate-solubilizing and potash-mobilizing microorganisms for 
improving nutrient-use efficiency and soil health. Further, microbial biopesticides and bio-
control agents such as Trichoderma, Pseudomonas fluorescens, Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt), 
Beauveria bassiana, Metarhizium anisopliae and nucleopolyhedrovirus (NPV) have been 
developed for eco-friendly pest management. Further, genome editing research has been 
initiated by ICAR in 24 field crops and 17 horticultural crops covering 41 crops across 34 
research institutions. The Government of India has allocated ₹500 crore for genome editing 
research at ICAR in March 2024. Two genome-edited rice varieties, namely DRR Dhan 100 
(Kamala) and Pusa DST Rice 1, have been developed by ICAR. 
Bio-technology offers significant green growth prospects by enabling sustainable 
intensification of agriculture. It facilitates the development of climate-resilient crops and 
improves resource-use efficiency. It also helps in reducing dependence on synthetic 
agrochemicals and promotes environmentally sustainable farming practices. These 
technologies, when integrated with conventional breeding, good agronomic practices and 
appropriate biosafety and regulatory frameworks, are expected to contribute towards 
enhanced productivity, conservation of natural resources, environmental sustainability, 
improvement in farmers’ income and long-term food and nutritional security.  
As reported by ICAR, to address the challenges posed by increasing population, 
climate change and declining natural resources, biotechnology, along with conventional 
breeding and improved crop management practices, provides opportunities for sustainable 
agricultural development. It enables the development of high-yielding and climate-resilient 
crop varieties. It also helps in improving nutrient and water-use efficiency and strengthening 
pest and disease management. Further, it promotes the use of bio-fertilizers and bio-control 
agents for sustainable agricultural production.

(b) the number of inspections conducted, cases registered, prosecutions launched and convictions

(a) to (e) The Central Government has notified the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Pet Shop) 
Rules, 2018, the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Dog Breeding and Marketing) Rules, 2017, 
the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Regulation of Livestock Markets) Rules, 20 17, the 
Transport of Animals Rules, 1978 (as amended), and the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Egg 
Laying Hens) Rules, 2023, which prescribe welfare standards for the housing, sale, transport and 
handling of different categories of animals. Further, The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972  is 
enacted to provide protection of wild animals, birds and plants. Species specified in Schedules I 
and II of the Act are accorded a high degree of protection against hunting and other prohibited 
activities. Matters relating to illegal trade in wild animals and protected birds are dealt with under 
the provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. 
The implementation and enforcement of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 and the 
above rules framed thereunder, as well as the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, are primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments/Union Territor y Administrations through 
their designated enforcement agencies. Accordingly, information relating to inspections 
conducted, cases registered, prosecutions launched and convictions secured in respect of illegal 
sale, transport and caging of birds and other  animals is maintained by the respective State 

Governments/Union Territory Administrations and the concerned enforcement agencies and is 
not maintained centrally by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 
The Government of India has reviewed the existing penalties under  Prevention of Cruelty to 
Animals Act, 1960 which is very low and not having deterrent effect. 
As per the information received from Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change 
(MoEF&CC), the important steps taken for protection and conservation of species include: 
a) The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 provides for punishment for violation of its 
provisions. The Act also provides for forfeiture of any equipment, vehicle or weapon that 
is used for committing wildlife offence. 
 
b) A network of Protected Areas have been created in the country for protection of wildlife, 
including birds and their habitat. 
 
c) Financial assistance is provided to State Governments /UT Administrations for 
management of wildlife and development of its habitat under the Centrally sponsored 
schemes ‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’  and ‘Project Tiger & Elephant’  of 
MoEF&CC.  
 
d) A specific component of ‘Recovery programme for saving critically endangered species 
and habitats’ is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Development 
of Wildlife Habitats’ of the MoEF&CC for focused conservation action on identified 25 
critically endangered species.  
 
e) Eco Development activities are undertaken by the States Governments /  UT 
administrations involving local communities in wildlife conservation.  
 
f) The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) has been set up under MoEF&CC to ensure 
co-ordination among various agencies and State Governments to combat organized 
wildlife crime. 
 
g) Advisories an d alerts are issued to State and Central agencies by the W CCB for  
preventive action on poaching and illegal wildlife trade.  
 
h) The law enforcement agencies like Border Security Force, Central Industrial Security 
Force, etc who assist in control of wildlife crime have been trained by the WCCB.

Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (PMKMDY) Scheme 
implemented by the Government across the country;  
(b) the total number of farmers benefitted under the said scheme in Maharashtra 
particularly in Latur, Ahilyanagar and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar districts, Madhya 
Pradesh particularly in Khandwa district and Dadra and Nagar Haveli Parliamentary 
Constituency;  
(c) whether there are still many farmers in the rural and remote areas of the above 
States who are not able to avail the benefits of the said scheme; and  
(d) if so, the reasons therefor along with the effective steps being taken by the 
Government to make the said scheme reach the deprived lanners? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):       Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY), a central sector scheme, 
is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for the entry age group of 18 to 40 
years with a provision of minimum monthly assured pension of ₹3000/- on attaining the 
age of 60 years, subject to exclusion criteria. The Scheme aims to create a social 
security net for the small and marginal farmers, who own cultivable land upto 2 
hectares as per the land records of the concerned State/UT, during their old age. The 

amount of the monthly contribution ranges between ₹55 to ₹200 per month depending 
upon the entry age of the farmers into the Scheme. Govt. of India also provides 
matching contribution in the pension account of the farmers. The Life Insurance 
Corporation (LIC) of India is the fund manager for the Scheme. 
 
(b) to (d): Under PM-KMY, 80,981 farmers are enrolled from the State of 
Maharashtra including 1870 in Latur district, 2595 in Ahilyanagar district, and 2609 in 
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. Further, 1,19,459 farmers are enrolled from the 
State of Madhya Pradesh, including 846 in Khandwa district, and 289 farmers are 
registered from The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. 
 
Various steps are taken to expand the coverage of PM-KMY Scheme in the rural 
and remote areas of all States/UTs including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and The 
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. As per the guidelines of the Scheme, 
the Common Service Centers (CSCs) are nominated for the enrollments of the farmers 
under the Scheme and a dedicated portal for PM-KMY Scheme has been created by 
the CSC to ensure smooth operations under the Scheme.  CSCs mobilize farmers, 
disseminate information and create awareness about the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
Maandhan Yojana (PMKMY), and facilitate enrolment of eligible farmers. Further, 
States/Union Territories are advised from time to time to undertake outreach activities 
for wider awareness of Government schemes and to maximize enrolment of eligible 
farmers under PMKMY.

Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities, exemplifies this vision with strong multimodal

PM GatiShakti to enhance logistics efficiency and competitiveness.

2666. Shri Sunil Bose: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the mechanism followed by the Government to assess the 
number of workers unable to register their attendance due to 
issues with the National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) 
attendance App; 
(b)  the details and total number of attendance discrepancies 
between the NMMS App and physical muster rolls since April 
2025 to till date, State-wise; 
(c)  the guidelines followed by the Government to ensure that no 
worker is denied wages due to issues with digital attendance 
recording on the NMMS App; and 
(d)  the details and total number of complaints filed regarding issues 
with the NMMS App alongwith the action taken thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): To ensure transparency and accountability in the 
implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS), it was decided that 
States/UTs shall ensure capturing of attendance at the worksite 
through National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) App with two-
time stamped, geo-tagged photographs of the workers in a day for all 
the works (except Individual Beneficiary Work) through NMMS w.e.f. 
1st January, 2023. A robust, face authentication based attendance 
capture mechanism using NMMS App has been adopted under Viksit 
Bharat- Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajivika Mission (Gramin) Act, which 
has come into force with effect from 01.07.2026.  
  
A comprehensive exemption mechanism has been put in place 
to ensure that no genuine worker faces difficulties due to technical 

Page 2 of 2 
 
issues in NMMS. Exemption mechanism ensures that in case of 
network connectivity issues at work site, attendance can be 
captured in offline mode, which can subsequently uploaded after 
moving into network connected area. Additionally exemptions are 
available in situations where the device or application is not 
functioning, eKYC of the workers has not been completed or the 
worker has a disability such as visual impairment. Any technical 
issues faced by States/UTs are taken up with the Ministry and are 
resolved on a real time basis. 
  
   The implementation of the NMMS application has significantly 
improved the attendance management system and the overall 
efficiency of the process. NMMS application also helps in timely 
payment of wages as wage lists and FTOs can be generated 
immediately after the closure of the muster roll. The States/UTs have 
clearly been advised to ensure that no eligible and willing workers be 
denied employment under above schemes due to any technical 
difficulties in NMMS.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण

(a)  whether the Government has undertaken any comprehensive review of the existing 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) system with regard to its coverage, effectiveness and 
regional disparities; 
(b)  the details of crops and States where procurement under MSP has remained 
significantly below production during the last three years, along with the reasons therefor; 
and 
(c)  the policy measures proposed to improve transparency, efficiency and timely 
payment under the MSP regime? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (c):  Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of 
the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the 
State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned.  

The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops 
with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production 
from year 2018-19 onwards. 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by 
Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government 
procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other 
designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, 
oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of 
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the 
concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these 
produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are 
National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National 
Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also 
procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute 
Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective 
State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, 
convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage 
and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and 
depots / godowns are also established at key points.  
The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process and during the last 
few years, procurement processes under MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP 
to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ 
procurement portals ensure that the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase.  
 National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog (erstwhile Planning 
Commission) has conducted a study entitled “Efficacy of minimum support prices on 
farmers”, 2016. The study covered 14 States, 36 Districts, 72 Blocks, 144 Villages and 
1440 Households. The study is based on both the primary and secondary data. The study 
has found among other things that MSP declared by the Government has encouraged 78 % 
of the farmers covered under the study for adopting improved methods of farming such as 

high yielding varieties of seeds, organic manure, chemical fertilizer, pesticides and 
improved methods of harvesting etc. 
Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data of 
procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The year wise details of procurement 
and MSP amount paid to farmers during 2023-24 to 2025-26 (upto June, 2026) are given as

(a) to (d) India’s export and import standard for Organic products is the National 
Programme for Organic Production (NPOP). India has a Mutual recognition 
Arrangement (MRA) on Organic standards with Australia, which is implemented with 
effect from 24.09.2025. With respect to New Zealand, an interim Mutual Recognition 
Arrangement (MRA) has been agreed, which shall come into effect, on the date of 
entry into force of the India-New Zealand FTA. 
  
The Government thr ough the Agricultural and Processed Food Products 
Development Authority(APEDA), which is the Secretariat for the NPOP, conducted 
detailed consultations with the key stakeholders including FSSAI for the revision of 
the NPOP Regulations, following which, the Eighth Edition of NPOP was notified on 
5th January 2025, which came into effect from 180 days from the issuance of this 
notification. 

2 
 
  
To strengthen the Organic legal and regulatory framework, so as to address non 
compliances including to curb counterfei t organic products and to protect the 
credibility of India's organic agricultural exports, stringent penalty provisions and 
sanctions have been introduced in the Eighth Edition of the NPOP, stipulating 
penalties for various forms of non -compliances by the certification bodies, certified 
operators etc. Penalty provisions have also been introduced against external service 
providers of Organic grower groups, as a further deterrent measure for various non-
compliances by them, including misrepresentation.  
  
Trade of organic products in the domestic market is covered under the Food Safety 
and Standards (Organic Food) Regulations, 2017 read with the Food Safety & 
Standards Act, 2006. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), 
under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, is the nodal agency for maintaining 
oversight over domestic organic trade, including enforcing compliance of standards, 
by the stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES  
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2670  
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
COASTAL EROSION AND CLIMATE-RESILIENT FISHING VILLAGES 
 
2670.    SHRI SASIKANTH SENTHIL: 
             SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has identified coastal fishing villages in Tamil Nadu under the Climate 
Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages initiative, if so, the names of such villages and districts 
selected in Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the amount of funds allocated, released and utilised for Tamil Nadu under the said initiative; 
(c) whether coastal erosion and climate vulnerability mapping ha s been used for selection of 
villages in Tamil Nadu; 
(d) the livelihood, housing, safety and infrastructure support proposed for fisherfolk in such 
villages; and 
(e) whether the Government has reviewed support for deep -sea fishing transition mariculture and 
coastal pilots, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (b): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
recognising the importance of strengthening coastal communities, has undertaken a transformative 
initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY ) to develop 100 existing 
coastal fishermen villages, located close to the coastline across all coastal States and Union 
Territories, including Tamil Nadu, into Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFVs). 
This initiative aims to upgrade these vi llages into economically vibrant and climate‑resilient 
fishermen villages. Under PMMSY, ₹200 crore has been earmarked for the development of 
CRCFVs, with a unit cost of ₹2 crore per village, with 100% funding by the Government of India. 
In Tamil Nadu, 16 coastal villages have been approved for development as CRCFVs at a total cost 
of ₹32 crore, and the first and second installments amounting to ₹16 crore have already been 
released to the State Government. The district‑wise details of the coastal villages identified in Tamil 
Nadu are furnished at Annexure‑I.  
 

(c) Villages for development as CRCFV across all coastal States/UTs, including Tamil Nadu, have 
been jointly identified with the respective State/UT Governments in accordance with the prescribed 
Guidelines. The selection of villages under CRCFV prioritized those situated on the seashore and 
close to the shoreline (0–5 km, then 0–10 km, then 0–20 km). Preference was given to villages with 
a higher proportion of fishermen (100%, then 90–100%, then 80–90%), greater numbers of fishing 
boats, fish landings, and allied fisheries activities. Alignment with the villages covered under the 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) Scheme of ICAR was also 
considered wherever available. 
(d) The De partment of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying has 
approved the need -based activities proposed by the State Government in the DPR submitted for 
each village. The activities include infrastructure components like multipurpose halls, fish auction 
and processing units, drying yards, net‑mending sheds, storage rooms, RCC roads with street 
lighting, desalination plants and rest sheds. The livelihood and economic interventions include 
marine and brackish‑water cage culture, bivalve and crab fattening units, bio‑fertilizer production, 
artificial reefs, ice boxes, fishing‑implement shops and mobile fish‑food outlets, green‑fuel boats, 
life buoys, life jackets and towing equipment, collectively aimed at strengthening resilience, 
enhancing productivity and improving welfare across coastal fishing communities.  
(e) The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has 
supported the transition from trawling to deep-sea fishing and towards mariculture to promote 
sustainable fishing practices under the Blue Revolution and PMMSY schemes. The Government of 
Tamil Nadu has reported that, under the Blue Revolution Scheme (2017 –18), the State undertook 
the “Diversification of trawl fishing boats from Palk Bay into deep‑s ea fishing boats”. Approval 
was accorded for replacing 750 trawlers with deep‑sea fishing vessels at a unit cost of ₹80 lakh, 
with a financial support comprising 50% central subsidy, 20% State subsidy, 10% beneficiary 
contribution, and 20% institutional financing, amounting to ₹281.50 crore.  
For mariculture, financial assistance has been extended under the PMMSY Scheme for activities 
such as seaweed culture (raft and monoline methods) and open sea cage farming across multiple 
districts of Tamil Nadu . These  efforts have benefited over 2000 fisherfolks and supported the 
establishment of nearly 10,000 seaweed raft/monoline uni

Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of Tied Grants allocated under the Fifteenth Finance Commission from 2020-21 to 
2025-26, year, State and UT-wise; 
  
(b) the details of Tied Grants allocated, released and utilised under the Fifteenth Finance 
Commission during said period, State, year and district-wise, Mandal-wise and Gram Panchayat-
wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
  
(c) the component-wise details of expenditure incurred under the Drinking Water and 
Sanitation/Solid Waste Management components out of the Tied Grants during the said period, 
State and district-wise, Mandal-wise, Gram Panchayat-wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
  
(d) the details of works undertaken and completed under the said components during the said 
period, State and district-wise, Mandal-wise and Gram Panchayat-wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
  
(e) whether any unutilised funds, delays in utilisation/implementation gaps have been reported 
under the Tied Grants in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof, district-wise; and 
  
(f) the steps taken/proposed to ensure timely utilisation and effective monitoring of Tied Grants 
under the Fifteenth Finance Commission in Andhra Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) to (f) The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti is the nodal 
Department for the implementation of the Fifteenth Finance Commission Tied Grants.  
  
As reported by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, the Fifteenth Finance 
Commission submitted its report in two phases, the first, an Interim Report for the financial year 
2020-21 and Final Report for the award period 2021-26.  
  

2 
 
The Fifteenth Finance Commission (FC-XV) recommended Rs.2.36 lakh crore to RLBs in 28 
States including Andhra Pradesh for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26 including for those areas 
which are not required to have panchayats (Fifth and Sixth Scheduled areas and excluded areas), 
out of which 60% i.e. Rs. 1.42 lakh crore is tied grant to be utilized for (i) supply of drinking 
water, rainwater harvesting and water recycling; and, (ii) sanitation and maintenance of ODF 
status equally i.e. Rs. 0.71 Lakh crore for each component. 
  
The release of tied grant allocated to all states is based on the fulfilment of stipulated criteria 
mentioned in the operational guideline for the implementation of XV-FC recommendation on 
RLB grants. Department of Expenditure further release funds to states and state government 
transferred the same to RLBs/ Excluded areas. The tied grant has to be utilized specifically for 
Water and Sanitation related activities as mentioned in the manual for utilization for tied grant.

(a) to (d): State Governments adopt different policy measures to promote industrial 
development. The Union Government supplements the efforts of the State/UT 
Governments through various schemes, programmes, and policy initiatives for 
the overall development and promotion of industry across the Country, 
including Punjab. 
During the last 4 years, Amritsar district has received investments amounting 
to ₹8,706 crore through the Fast Track Single Window Portal with potential 
employment generation of 32,069 persons. These investments span various 
sectors including Agri & Food Processi ng, Agro -based Industries (including 
Processing of Agro-waste), Tourism & Hospitality. 

Amritsar qualifies as a Border District under Punjab Industrial & Business 
Development Policy, 2026. The Policy provides an enhanced fiscal incentive 
framework for indus trial units established therein. The incentives available 
under this framework include Capital Investment Incentive, Interest Subsidy, 
Net SGST reimbursement, Employment Generation Subsidy, Stamp Duty 
exemption/reimbursement, Change of Land Use (CLU) fee e xemption, and 
Electricity Duty exemption, among others, subject to the terms and conditions 
prescribed under the Policy. Eligible units in Amritsar may avail an overall fiscal 
incentive ceiling of up to 125% (which is higher than the ceilings of incentives  
available in other districts) of the eligible Fixed Capital Investment (FCI), subject 
to a maximum of ₹500 crore, along with a flexible eligibility period of 10 to 15 
years. 
The Government of India has approved development of Integrated 
Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at Rajpura-Patiala with an area of 1,098.85 acres 
under the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) in August 2024 for total 
project cost of Rs. 1,367.72 crore. Project Manager for New Cities (PMNC) and 
EPC Contractor have been appointed for implementation of internal trunk 
infrastructure works. As per DPR, Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at 
Rajpura-Patiala under the Amritsar -Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) has an 
estimated employment generation potential of approximately 64,200 jobs. 
The Punjab Industrial & Business Development Policy, 2026 identifies Agri & 
Food Processing Industries and Processing of Agro -waste into 
Energy/Bioenergy/Manure as Priority Sectors, with enhanced fiscal support 
available to eligible units established in Border Districts, including Amritsar. 
In addition, the Punjab Food Processing Policy, 2026 provides sector -specific 
incentives such as 100% exemption of Mandi  Fee/Market Fee/Rural 
Development Fee and other State taxes on the purchase of raw material for 
eligible food processing units for a period of five years, along with 100% Net 
SGST reimbursement, subject to prescribed conditions. 
The Punjab Tourism & Hospit ality Policy, 2026 has also been notified to  
promote tourism-linked economic activity in the region. These measures are 
aimed at leveraging Amritsar's tourism potential to generate allied 
manufacturing and service-sector employment in the border region.

advised on the timely and need-based application of recommended insecticides and

 Shri Bhumare Sandipanrao Asaram: 
 Dr. Shivaji Bandappa Kalge: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to increase the number of 
guaranteed work days under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for 
Rojgar and Aajeevika Mission-Gramin (VB-GRAM-G); 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to launch any new 
programmes to generate permanent employment opportunities 
in the rural areas of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to provide additional 
financial assistance to women Self Help Groups (SHGs) under

and Madhya Pradesh and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (c): Consequent upon commencement of the Viksit Bharat– 
Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) 
Act, 2025, the scheme has successfully been implemented in rural 
areas of the entire country w.e.f 01.07.2026. The VB-G RAM G 
provides for a statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty five 
days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household 
whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work 
against one hundred day of guaranteed wage employment available 
under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The new scheme has been 
successfully implemented in the State of Maharashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh also w.e.f 0.1.07.2026. In case of Maharashtra n interim

allocation Rs.4420.32 crore has been made for the State. 
Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.1459.92 Crore have 
been issued to the State of Maharashtra as first installment of Central 
Share under various components based on the proposal received from 
the State. Further in case of Madhya Pradesh an interim allocation 
Rs.6252.03 crore has been made for the State. Subsequently, Mother 
Sanctions amounting to Rs.630.76 Crore have been issued to the 
State of Madhya Pradesh as first installment of Central Share under 
various components based on the proposal received from the State.  
It is also stated that under Section 5(4) of the Act, the State 
Governments may make provision for providing additional days of 
employment beyond the period guaranteed under the Act from their 
own resources. The Act also aims to strengthen sustainable rural 
livelihoods through the creation of durable assets and 
implementation of the permissible works specified in Schedule I of 
the Act, namely Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, 
Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works to Mitigate 
Extreme Weather Events. These provisions are intended to enhance 
livelihood security, strengthen rural infrastructure and promote 
sustainable rural development.  
(d): Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM), a flagship poverty alleviation programme of the 
Ministry of Rural Development, is being implemented through the 
State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) across 760 districts and 
7,246 blocks in 34 States and Union Territories including Maharashtra 
and Madhya Pradesh. As of June 2026, the Mission has mobilized 
about 10.08 crore rural households into nearly 92 lakh Self Help 
Groups (SHGs). Under the existing provisions of DAY-NRLM, 
capitalization support is provided to eligible SHGs in the form of 
Revolving Fund (RF) of ₹20,000–₹30,000 per SHG and Community 
Investment Fund (CIF) of up to ₹2.50 lakh per SHG to support income-
generating and livelihood activities, including entrepreneurial 
ventures. 
  In addition, interest subvention is available on bank loans to 
eligible SHGs. For loans up to ₹3 lakh, banks provide credit at a 
concessional interest rate of 7% per annum. For loans above ₹3 lakh 
and up to ₹5 lakh, banks extend credit at an interest rate equivalent 
to their one-year MCLR or any other external benchmark-based 
lending rate or 10% per annum, whichever is lower. Cumulatively, 
loans amounting to ₹13.41 lakh crore have been disbursed to SHGs 
under the Mission. These benefits are available to eligible SHGs, 
including those in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, in accordance 
with the scheme guidelines.

2686. SHRI P C MOHAN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether any company approved or applying under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of 
Electric Passenger Cars in India has proposed to set up or expand manufacturing facilities in 
Karnataka, including Bengaluru and if so, the details thereof including investment committed;  
 
(b) the details of domestic value addition and technology transfer commitments applicable to any 
such facility proposed in Karnataka, and the timeline for achieving the prescribed localisation levels;  
 
(c) the details of m anufacturing capacity and employment generation expected to be created in 
Karnataka under the Scheme; and  
 
(d) the role envisaged for the State Government of Karnataka in facilitating land, infrastructure and 
other support for such investment under the Scheme's implementation framework? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (c): Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India (SPMEPCI) 
was notified on 15.03.2024 to attract investments from global electric passenger car manufacturers 
and promote India as a manufacturing destination for electric passenger cars. T o avail benefit under 
SPMEPCI, approved applicants have to setup manufacturing facilities in India with a minimum 
investment of Rs. 4,150 cr, for manufacturing of e -4W and made operational within a period of 3 
years from the date of issuance of approval le tter by MHI and achieve minimum Domestic Value 
Addition (DVA) of 25% within 3 year & 50% within 5 year.  
 
Application window for SPMEPCI was open for 120 days till 21.10.2025, however, no 
applications were received.

specified in SPMEPCI notification dated 15.03.2024 were issued on 02.06.2025 and State 
Government has no role w.r.t duty foregone benefit under SPMEPCI. However, State Governments 
can facilitate setting up o f manufacturing facilities along with other initiatives for ease of doing 
business to attract foreign investment.

(a)        The status of implementation of recently concluded Free Trade Agreements

(b)      FTAs are economic instruments aimed at expanding trade, enhancing 
competitiveness and deepening economic integration. FTAs provide calibrated market 
access through tariff elimination at Entry into Force (EIF), ph ased tariff 
reductions/elimination, and sensitive/exclusion lists across sectors. The details of 
sectors covered, tariffs structure and salient features of the implemented FTAs may be 
sourced at https://www.commerce.gov.in/#/international-trade/trade-agreements   
Assessment of the impact of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) is an ongoing exercise . 
India's recently concluded Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with Australia, the UAE, 
EFTA, Oman, the UK and New Zealand are expected to provide opportunities for 
enhanced trade and growth of domestic industries. These agreements include 
provisions relating to investment and market access, which is expected to support 
domestic producti on, facilitate investment flows, and create opportunities for 
employment across labour intensive sectors including manufacturing, agriculture, 
MSMEs and allied sectors

specific stakeholder consultations are held at all stages of the negotiations. FTAs are 
negotiated with the endeavour to deliver comprehensive, balanced, fair and mutually 
beneficial outcomes. It also enables a preferential, stable and predictable trade 
ecosystem for Indian exporters in the trading partner countries. In addition to this 
structured approach, post -implementation, the Government is continuously engaged 
with all stakeholders to ensure effective FTA utilization through trade promotion, trade 
facilitation and addressing challenges if any. Strategic safeguards for sensitive sectors 
ensure export growth while protecting domestic priorities. 
 (c)      Government has taken several initiatives and measures, from time to time,

Promotion Mission (EPM) for the period FY 2025 –26 to FY 2030 –31, aimed at

o Niryat Prothsahan, focused on improving access to trade finance through 
instruments such as interest subvention, export factoring, collater al 
guarantees for export credit, credit guarantee for e -commerce exporters, 
and credit enhancement support; and 
o Niryat Disha, focused on other trade enablers such as export quality and 
compliance support, international branding and packaging, market access 
initiatives, export logistics & warehousing, and trade intelligence. 
  
(iii)       Bharat Trade Net (BTN): Bharat Trade Net (BTN), announced in the Union 
Budget 2025 is a flagship digital public infrastructure initiative to enhances MSME 
competitiveness by enabling simpler, paperless documentation, reducing compliance 
burdens, and facilitating faster, secure trade transactions recognized globally. 
  
(iv)       The introduction of grassroots programs such as Districts as Export Hubs

MSME exporters by easing supply chain bottlenecks.

Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the projects approved, investment received, production capacity, employment 
generation and technology development achieved so far for the manufacturing of flex -fuel vehicles, 
electric vehicles and related automobile components under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
Scheme, category-wise and State-wise;  
 
(b) whether the Government has formulated any phased national policy to incentivize flex -fuel 
vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than twenty per cent ethanol and if so, the details 
thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any independent cost -benefit study regarding the 
incentivization of flex-fuel and electric vehicles and if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any integrated scientific study on the impact of ethanol 
production on water consumption, agricultural land use, food security, carbon emissions, biofuel 
supply chain and the domestic automobile industry and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a):   Production Linked Incentive scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (PLI-Auto scheme) 
is implemented on an all-India basis. The current status of implementation of PLI-Auto scheme is as 
below:-

(d): Government has adopted a balanced approach to the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) 
Programme, ensuring that water sustainability, food security and farmers' interests remain paramount. 
Under the National Policy on Biofuels, ethanol is produced from multiple ap proved feedstocks, 
including sugarcane-based feedstocks, maize, damaged foodgrains, broken rice, foodgrains unfit for 
human consumption, surplus foodgrains approved by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee 
(NBCC) and other approved agricultural feedstocks. 
Government is also promoting crop diversification towards comparatively less water -
intensive feedstocks such as maize. An Expert Committee constituted by Ministry of Agriculture & 
Farmers Welfare in 2024 examined the water requirement of various eth anol feedstock crops & its 
recommendations are being considered while implementing the programme. 
 
Water-use efficiency is also being enhanced through micro-irrigation, drip irrigation and other 
water conservation measures under the Per Drop More Crop component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi 
Sinchayee Yojana. Many sugar mills are also encouraging farmers to adopt water-efficient cultivation 
practices.  
 
Molasses-based distilleries with incineration boilers and grain -based distilleries are required 
to operate as Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) units, enabling recycling and reuse of process water while 
eliminating liquid effluent discharge.

2690. SHRI DHARMENDRA YADAV: 
  
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री ) be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number of sanctioned posts reserved for the persons belonging to 
 Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes 
 (OBCs) in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry an d its subordinate offices 
 organisations and autonomous bodies; 
(b) the total number of posts lying vacant out of the said posts at present; 
(c) the number of backlog vacancies for persons belonging to SCs, STs, and OBCs; 
 and 
(d) the action being taken by the Government to fill up the said vacancies and 
 backlog posts? 
  
  
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) The Ministry of Commerce and Industry comprises of two Departments namely 
Department of Commerce (DoC) and Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal 
Trade (DPIIT) which have officers belonging to All India Service, Central Secretariat 
Service, Indian Economic Services, Indian Statistics Service, Central Secretariat 
Stenographers Service, Indian Trade Service and other organized services. The 
guidelines of Government of India regarding reservation to Scheduled Caste (SCs), 
Scheduled Tribes (ST s) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) are followed by the 
respective Cadre Controlling Authorities. However, for the posts which are filled by 
Department/ Subordinate Offices /Autonomous Bodies itself, the reservation to 
SC/ST/OBC categories is ensured by maintaining appropriate reservation roster. In this 
regard, Liaison Officers have been appointed by both the Departments to monitor proper 
implementation of reservation in their respective organizations including Subordinate 
Offices Organizations and Autonomous Bodies. 
  
Occurrence and filling up of vacancies, along with backlog reserved vacancies, 
is a continuous process. By the time, vacant posts are filled up, new vacancies arise 
due to retirement, resignation, death, promotion etc. These vacancies are fi lled up by 
various recruiting agencies viz. Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff 
Selection Commission (SSC) and by the Department/Organisations in accordance with 
the reservations norms/guidelines of Government of India for providing reservations to 
SC/ST/OBC categories.

2695. SHRI PARIMAL SUKLABAIDYA:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the progress made in the implementation of the PM E -DRIVE Scheme in Assam, particularly in 
Cachar district, including the number of electric vehicles registered and reimbursement claims 
processed;  
 
(b) the details of public EV charging stations sanctioned, installed and operational in Cachar district 
and along the Guwahati–Silchar highway and other major corridors in Assam;  
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the fuel savings and reduction in carbon dioxide emissions 
achieved through electric vehicle adoption in Assam, particularly in Cachar district; and  
 
(d) the steps taken to promote electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and encourage the 
adoption of electric public t ransport and commercial vehicles in Cachar district and other parts of 
Assam? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): The PM E -DRIVE Scheme is being implemented on a pan -India basis, and no State -wise 
allocation of funds has been made. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 42,035 EVs have been sold in Assam, 
under this Scheme which includes 8,003 EVs sold in Cachar district. Furth er, a total of 40,009 EVs 
have been incentivised in Assam with a total reimbursement of  ₹ 99.10 crore to OEMs.  
 
(b): An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment 
of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including the state of Assam.  
Assam has not yet submitted any proposal for deployment of EVPCS under the PM E -DRIVE 
scheme.    
 
(c): No such assessment has been done by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI)  for Cachar 
district of Assam. 
 
(d): The MHI is implementing following schemes to promote electric mobility, strengthen 
charging infrastructure and encourage the adoption of electric public transport  and commercial 
vehicles across the country including Cachar district and other parts of Assam: 
 
i. Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) 
Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 
01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided 
demand incentive for e -2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e -buses and setting up of EV public 
charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric 
vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e -4Ws. In addition, 5, 297 electric buses (e -buses) have 
been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was 
allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. 

 
ii. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry 
in India (PLI -Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for 
Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of 
₹25,938 crore.  
 
iii. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced 
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.2021  notified the PLI  
Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The 
scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC 
batteries. 
 
iv. PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: 
This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore is implemented from 01.04.2024 . This scheme 
supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e -2W, e-
3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e -Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV 
PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation of 
₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e -buses out of which 
13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e -buses have been 
approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for 
deployment of EV Public Charging Stations on pan India basis.   
 
v. PM e -Bus Sewa -Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme : This Scheme notified on 
28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 
electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e -bus operators in 
case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs).

(a) to (c): The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India 
continuously undertakes nationwide campaigns and awareness programmes in 
collaboration with the State Governments and with active involvement of Agriculture 
Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Indian Council of Agricultural Research 
and Krishi Vigyan Kendras to educate farmers on modern agricultural practices and 
enhance crop productivity, production and farmers income.  
  

 
 
       Under Sub-Mission on Agriculture Extension (SMAE), a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme “Support to State Extension Programs for Extension Reforms” (Agricultural 
Technology Management Agency-ATMA) is being implemented by the Government 
of India in 734 districts of 28 states & 5 UTs for promoting decentralized and farmer-
friendly extension system in the country since 2005-06. The Scheme supports State 
Government’s efforts and to make available latest agricultural technologies and good 
agricultural practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and allied areas 
(Including improving crop productivity and exposure to modern agricultural practices) 
to farmers to modernize agriculture through different extension activities viz; Farmers 
Training, Demonstrations, Exposure Visits, Kisan Mela, Mobilization of Farmers 
Groups and organizing Farm Schools etc. Under this Scheme, it has been 
provisioned that at least 50% beneficiaries must be selected from Small & Marginal 
farmer category. 
 
   During the financial year 2025-26, 50.92 lakh farmers have been benefitted 
through different extension activities under the ATMA Scheme.  
 
      The Mass Media Support to Agriculture Extension Scheme creates awareness 
among farming communities and other stakeholders through the dissemination of 
information on DA&FW schemes, crop advisories, weather and market information, 
and region-specific modern agricultural technologies. The scheme leverages 
Doordarshan, All India Radio and digital and social media platforms to ensure wider 
outreach, timely access to knowledge and effective dissemination of farmer-centric 
information. 
      To educate farmers, the Ministry supports and organizes national/regional-level 
exhibitions/fairs to create awareness about various schemes, missions and new 
initiatives, while promoting appropriate technologies, improved agronomic practices 
and best practices among farmers and other stakeholders in the agriculture and 
allied sectors.  
     In addition, the Department operates Kisan Helpline Centres to provide a single-
window platform for farmers’ on agricultural advisories, information on Government 
schemes/programmes and grievance redressal.  
  

 
  
     Bharat-VISTAAR (Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources) 
is a multilingual AI-powered Digital Public Infrastructure platform designed to provide 
farmers with reliable, real-time and location-specific agricultural advisories and 
access to various farmer support services. The platform integrates information on 
Government schemes, benefit status tracking, grievance redressal, weather updates, 
mandi prices, ICAR advisories and other agricultural services to enable informed 
decision-making and better crop management.

flagship Schemes/Missions on crop diversification, organic farming and value 
addition, including Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH),

a) The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying  (DAHD), Government of India  has 
successfully conducted Pashujanya Yudh Abhyas (PYA), on animal health emergencies, at Khari 
village, Vidisha District, Madhya Pradesh, from 29th June 2026 to 3rd July 2026. The evaluation

preparedness, coordination and communication mechanisms, and emergency response capabilities 
for managing zoonotic disease outbreaks. 
(b) and (c) The exercise provided an opportunity to identify the gaps in outbreak preparedness and 
response. Accordingly, it helped in strengthening the areas like timely communication, 
coordination, sampling and testing protocols, infection prevention and control, waste disposal, 
capacity building of response teams, documentation and information sharing across stakeholders. 
The exercise also highlighted the importance of continued capacity building and adherence to 
standard operating procedures.  

(d) The measures taken by the department to strengthen preparedness for future zoonotic disease 
outbreaks include: 
i. Under Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) financial assistance is 
provided to States/UTs for training and awareness on Good Animal Husbandry Practices, 
Biosecurity/Sanitary measures, vaccination against animal diseases, disease surveillance a nd 
monitoring and capacity building which supports preparedness and response for disease 
management and outbreaks. 
ii. Department under the component of Assistance to States for Control of Animal Disease 
(ASCAD) of LHDCP supports States/UTs on sharing basis for State prioritised activities  such as 
capacity building, surveillance and monitoring of livestock diseases, training, prevention and 
control of zoonotic diseases including emergent and re-emergent diseases etc.  
iii. Formulated National Action Plan for Prevention, Control and Containment of Avian Influenza 
for preparedness and response including surveillance, biosecurity, culling operation, movement 
control, and post-operation monitoring. 
iv. The ‘Standard Veterinary Treatment Guidelines (SVTGs) has been developed for Livestock 
and Poultry’ for best practices in veterinary care to enhance livestock health and disease control 
while ensuring the responsible use of drugs including antimicrobials.  
v. Formulated the Crisis Management Plan (CMP) for Livestock Diseases’ for managing and 
responding to animal disease outbreaks, ensuring swift containment, mitigation and handling of 
animal health crises and reducing pandemic risks through prevention and control measures. 
vi. Advisories related to emergent infectious and zoonotic diseases issued to all States/UTs from 
time to time.  
vii. Formulated the National Action Plan for Control and Eradication for Glanders for prevention 
and control and containment of disease in definite time line.   
viii. The Department supports five designated Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratories (RDDLs) 
and one Central Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (CDDL) for specialized and referral diagnostic 
services for livestock diseases. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for laboratory 
investigations, including sample collection, preservation and dispatch, are in place to promote 
uniformity and quality in laboratory diagnostics. 
ix. The Indian Council of Agricultural Research Research – National Institute of High Security 
Animal Diseases (ICAR -NIHSAD), Bhopal, functions as the national reference laboratory for 
emerging and exotic livestock and poultry diseases.

RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN 
  
2710.   SHRI G LAKSHMINARAYANA: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the number of agencies, institutions or vendors penalised, de-empanelled or blacklisted under 
RGSA during the last three years, State-wise; 
(b) the mechanisms adopted for verification of attendance and utilisation of funds under RGSA 
training programmes; 
(c) the particularly Andhra Pradesh district-wise, Gram Panchayats generating Own Source 
Revenue (OSR) exceeding the prescribed threshold during the last three years, State-wise; 
(d) whether any assessment has been conducted regarding the effectiveness of RGSA capacity-
building programmes, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(e) the measures taken to ensure authenticity of geo-tagged monitoring of Gram Panchayat assets 
and infrastructure projects? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. However, the Ministry of 
Panchayati Raj has been implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram 
Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/UTs. No agencies, 
institutions or vendors have been penalised, de-empanelled or blacklisted under Rashtriya Gram 
Swaraj Abhiyan during the last three years. 
(b) To ensure transparency, accountability, and accuracy in capacity-building activities under the 
Revamped RGSA, the Ministry has developed a dedicated Training Management Portal (TMP) 
for real-time monitoring of training programmes across States and Union Territories. The system 
incorporates Aadhaar-authenticated/biometric attendance, real-time upload of geo-tagged and 
time-stamped training photographs, and unique participant ID mapping to monitor training 
participation and prevent duplicate or proxy attendance. 

2 
 
Further, the utilization of funds under the RGSA Scheme is strictly governed by the Ministry of 
Finance guidelines through a robust financial monitoring framework. Funds are released and 
tracked in real time via the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) under the Single 
Nodal Agency (SNA/SNA-SPARSH) model, ensuring that further releases are made only after 
proper accounting of unspent balances. Additionally, the release of subsequent installments is 
contingent upon the submission of Utilization Certificates (UCs), audited accounts, and 
Quarterly/Annual Progress Reports (QPRs/APRs). 
(c) As per Article 243H of the Constitution of India, legislature of the State may, by law, 
authorize a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls and fees in 
accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits and assign to the Panchayats such 
taxes, duties, tolls and fees levied and collected by the State Government for such purposes and 
subject to such conditions and limits as may be specified in the law. As such, this Ministry does 
not maintain or monitor the district-wise status of Own Source Revenue (OSR) mobilization by 
Gram Panchayats (GPs) in States, including the State of Andhra Pradesh. However, as reported 
by the State of Andhra Pradesh, the district-wise details of OSR generated from FY 2023-24 to 
2025-26 is at Annexure-I. 
(d) Yes, Sir. To assess the effectiveness of RGSA capacity-building programmes and to propose 
corrective measures to strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions, an external evaluation of the 
Revamped RGSA has been undertaken through the Institute of Rural Management, Anand 
(IRMA). In addition, NITI Aayog has commissioned an independent assessment of RGSA to 
provide complementary evidence on outcomes. The evaluations indicate that the scheme’s 
structured, multi-layered capacity-building, combining classroom/thematic modules, exposure 
visits, and digital learning, has enhanced PRI capacities in Panchayat operations, planning, and 
implementation (including GPDP), digital governance, citizen engagement, and financial 
management. Post-training assessments record measurable gains in knowledge and practice, 
supporting more effective local governance and the localisation of SDGs.  
  
(e) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj ensures the authenticity of geo-tagged monitoring of Gram 
Panchayat assets and infrastructure projects through the mActionSoft mobile application. The 
application allows only live, real-time photo capture and does not allow uploading of pre-
existing gallery images. It automatically captures tamper-proof GPS coordinates and time stamps 
with each photograph and facilitates geo-tagging of assets at three stages of execution, namely 
before commencement, during progress, and upon completion. Geo-tagged photographs are 
linked with the corresponding asset/work in eGramSwaraj, enabling effective monitoring and 
verification.

Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details and total number of person-days generated under 
Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rojgar and Aajeevika Mission-
Gramin (VB-GRAM-G) scheme in Assam since 2025 with a 
special category for flood-affected and remote districts in 
Assam, district-wise; 
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under VB-
GRAM-G in Assam since 2025, year-wise; 
(c)  whether the transition to the VB-GRAM-G will address issues 
such as declining person days, wage delays, and seasonal 
disruptions in flood-prone regions like Assam, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d)  the manner in which such issues will be addressed, if not, the 
reasons therefor; and 
(e)  whether any region-specific reforms or flood-resilient works are 
being planned to ensure sustained rural employment generation 
in the States of the North-Eastern Region, if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Consequent upon enactment of Viksit Bharat–Guarantee 
for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Act 2025, 
the scheme has been operationalized in rural areas of the entire 
country with effect from 1st July, 2026 including Assam. District-wise 
details of persondays generated under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS and 
VB–G RAM G Scheme in the State of Assam, during the last financial 
years and current financial year 2026-27 (as on 30.07.2026) are at 
Annexure. 
  

Page 2 of 3 
 
With regard to fund allocation under VB- G RAM G, which came 
into force w.e.f 01.07.2026, it is stated that for FY 2026-27, an interim 
allocation Rs.1929.70 crore has been made for the State. 
Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.630.96 Crore have 
been issued to the State as first installment of Central Share under 
various components based on the proposal received, out of which the 
State has so far utilised an amount of Rs.18.58 Crore. 
  
(c) to (e): The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika 
Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 provides for a statutory 
guarantee of one hundred and twenty five days of wage employment 
in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members 
volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work, as against one 
hundred days under the erstwhile Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The Act 
also provides for technology-enabled implementation, timely 
payment of wages in accordance with the prescribed timelines, 
payment of delay compensation wherever applicable, and a time-
bound grievance redressal mechanism. 
Under VB–G RAM G Scheme, climate resilience, adaptation, and 
mitigation of extreme weather risks form an integral part of the 
statutory rural employment and asset creation framework. Within the 
planning framework, climate resilience and adaptation are embedded 
as core priorities under the Scheme. Permissible and priority 
categories of works include water conservation, watershed 
development, groundwater recharge, afforestation, source 
sustainability, flood and drought mitigation measures, and 
restoration and strengthening of natural resource assets. The 
Schedule to the Act further provides a dedicated thematic areas of 
works related to “Special works to mitigate Extreme Weather Events 
and Disaster Preparedness,” with an explicit thematic focus on 
disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, and protection of rural 
communities and assets from floods, cyclones, storms, droughts, 
landslides, forest fires, and other extreme weather events. 
Illustrative works under this category include construction of 
cyclone shelters, flood shelters, and multipurpose disaster-resilient 
structures; diversion channels, embankments, and other disaster-
mitigation works; stabilising ponds and water structures for flood 
management; post-disaster rehabilitation and restoration of rural 
roads and community assets windbreak and shelter-belt plantations; 
and forest fire management works such as fire breaks and fuel buffer 
zones. The intended outcome of these provisions is the creation of 
climate-resilient villages capable of withstanding extreme weather 
conditions.

(a) to (d): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated 
agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of the 
Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the State 
Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned. 
The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops 
with a minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from 
year 2018-19 onwards. 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by 
Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government 
procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other 
designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, 
oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of Pradhan 
Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the concerned 
State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these produce fall below 

the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural 
Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National Co-operative 
Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also procured by 
Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India 
(JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective State 
Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, convenience 
of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage and transportation 
etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and depots / godowns are 
also established at key points. The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process 
and during the last few years, procurement processes under MSP have improved to ensure 
payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and land records 
with the States’ procurement portals ensure that the farmers directly get the benefits of the 
MSP purchase.  
Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to reduce 
import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses. To encourage domestic production 
of pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad and Masur under the PM-

STEEL SCRAP RECYCLING UNITS IN TELANGANA  
 
 
2715. SHRI ARVIND DHARMAPURI:  
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of steel scrap recycling capacity created and quantity of steel scrap 
recycled in the country, State/UT-wise including Telangana;  
 
(b) the steps taken to promote organised scrap collection, processing and use of scrap 
in steelmaking;  
 
(c) whether any organised vehicle scrapping, steel recycling or downstream scrap-
based units have been established or proposed in Telangana; and  
 
(d) if so, the strategy adopted to reduce emissions, improve resource efficiency and 
build a circular economy in the steel sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)&(c): During Financial Year 2025-26, about 36 million tonnes ferrous scrap 
was used for production of steel, of which approximately 28 million tonnes scrap 
generated domestically.  The details of Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities 
(RVSFs) across the country including Telangana is available on the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways’ parivahan portal at the URL given below:  
 
‘https://vscrap.parivahan.gov.in/vehiclescrap/vahan/rvsfdetails.xhtml’. 
 
(b)&(d): The steps taken by the Government to promote organized scrap 
collection, processing and use in steelmaking to promote circular economy in the steel 
sector as well as the strategy adopted to reduce emissions and improve energy 
efficiency in the sector are as under: - 
 
(i)   The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy, 2019 provides a coordination 
framework with various Ministries to promote recycling of ferrous scrap generated 
from various sources. 
Contd…..2/- 

::2:: 
 
(ii)  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has formulated 
the Vehicle Scrapping Policy that includes a system of incentives/disincentives for 
creation of an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. Under the 
policy, MoRTH has issued rules for Registration and Functions of Vehicle 
Scrapping Facility (RVSF), which provides the procedures and infrastructure 
facilities required for de-pollution and dismantling of End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) 
for further recovery of metal and other materials under environmental regulations.  
 
(iii)  The Government of India has notified the Hazardous and Other Wastes 
(Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 to ensure safe 
handling, storage, recycling, utilisation, treatment and disposal of hazardous and 
other wastes in an environmentally safe manner. 
 
(iv)  Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change has introduced the 
Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025, which establishes a 
framework for managing End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) in an environmentally sound 
manner and mandates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), requiring vehicle 
producers to meet annual scrapping targets based on the type of vehicle and 
materials recovered. 
 
(v)  Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 has been notified by Ministry of Shipping, 
Ports and Waterways with aims to regulate and promote the safe and 
environmentally sound recycling of ships. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Steel has released the Taxonomy for Green Steel for defining 
and categorizing the low emission steel. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Steel released a report titled "Greening the Steel Sector in 
India: Roadmap and Action Plan" on the basis of the recommendations of the 14 
Task Forces constituted by this Ministry for this purpose which provides the 
roadmap for green steel and sustainability, towards net-zero target by 2070. The 
report is available on Ministry of Steel's website. 
 
(viii) Four pilot projects have been awarded for implementation of pilot 
projects for use of hydrogen in steel sector under National Green Hydrogen 
Mission launched by Ministry of New & Renewable Energy. 
 
(ix) National Solar Mission launched by Ministry of New and Renewable 
Energy in January, 2010 promotes the use of solar energy and also helps to 
reduce the emission of steel industry.  
 
(x)  Ministry of Power has notified Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) 
on 28.06.2023 for regulating Indian Carbon Market across various industrial 
sectors, which is also applicable to steel plants.

2718. Shri Sribharat Mathukumilli: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the number of eligible 
rural households in Andhra Pradesh excluded from Pradhan 
Mantri  Awas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) despite the revised 
eligibility criteria, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government has examined cases where landless 
eligible beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh were sanctioned 
houses but could not commence construction due to non-
availability of land, if so, the details and the action taken 
thereon; 
(c)  whether the Ministry has conducted any independent audits to 
assess the quality, durability and occupancy of PMAY-G houses 
constructed in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the findings and action 
taken on deficiencies; and 
(d)  whether the Government maintains data on PMAY-G 
beneficiaries who have migrated after receiving houses due to 
lack of livelihood opportunities, affecting the objective of 
sustainable rural habitation, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): Under PMAY-G, the universe of eligible beneficiaries includes 
all the houseless and households living in zero, one or two rooms with 
kutcha wall and kutcha roof (kutcha houses) as per Socio -Economic 
Caste Census (SECC) 2011 and Awaas+ 2018 survey data. The 
beneficiaries are identified on the basis of housing deprivation 
parameters and exclusion criteria prescribed under SECC 2011. 
These parameters/criteria are applied both on SECC 2011 and 
Awaas+ 2018 survey databases and then they are further subjected 
to due verification by Gram Sabha and an appellate process 

Page 2 of 3 
 
thereafter to arrive at the final list of eligible beneficiaries. In 
addition, the Government of India has provided approval for updating 
the Awaas + list for identifying additional eligible rural households 
using modified exclusion criteria under the scheme. In line with the 
decision of the Government of India, Awaas + 2024 Mobile App was 
launched for conducting the survey. To ensure that no eligible 
beneficiary is left behind, the Ministry of Rural Development has 
introduced Self Survey option also in the Awaas + 2024 Mobile App.  
  
(b): Providing land to the landless PMAY-G beneficiaries for the 
construction of houses is accorded top priority since they are among 
the most deserving beneficiaries in the Permanent Wait List (PWL) of 
PMAY-G. The responsibility to ensure that such beneficiaries are 
provided land vests with the state. The state can give land from the 
government pool of land or any other land, including public land 
(Panchayat common land, community land or land belonging to other 
local authorities).  
  
As informed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, some 
landless beneficiaries have been identified during the Awaas + 2024 
survey. Once Permanent Wait List on the basis of Awaas + 2024 
survey is finalised and enabled on AwaasSoft, the system will 
prioritise the beneficiaries as per the approved scheme guidelines. 
  
(c): Under PMAY-G, the house is constructed by the beneficiary 
himself/herself or under his/her supervision. Further, as per the 
guidelines of PMAY-G, the States/UTs provide the beneficiaries a 
bouquet of options of house designs according to the local climatic 
conditions, using appropriate local material and technology suitable 
to the region of their residence. The State/UT Government can also 
facilitate supply of construction material at competitive rates.  
 
The Ministry of Rural Development has also published a 
compendium of rural housing typologies “PAHAL” which is available 
on the program website of PMAY-G. This can also be accessed 
through AwaasApp. 
 
Further, to ensure good quality construction of houses under 
PMAY-G, the Government of India has rolled out the Rural Mason 
Training (RMT) Program with the target to train adequate number of 
masons for house construction in rural areas.  
 
(d): Data on PMAY-G beneficiaries who have migrated after 
receiving houses due to lack of livelihood opportunities is not 
maintained by the Ministry of Rural Development. However, as per the 

Page 3 of 3 
 
findings of an evaluation study of PMAY-G conducted by the Indian 
Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad, the incidence of 
migration among PMAY-G beneficiaries has declined by 
approximately 6%. The proportion of respondents citing “lack of 
housing” as a reason for migration has come down from 36% to 18%, 
and seasonal displacement has declined from 13.8% to 4.2%.
